articles.title: All-round boost for India ahead of Afghanistan T20Is; Jasprit Bumrah remains on track
articles.summary: Cricket News: India are set to get a major boost ahead of the T20I series against Afghanistan starting later this month. All-rounders Hardik Pandya and Nitish Kumar.
articles.body: India are set to get a major boost ahead of the T20I series against Afghanistan starting later this month. All-rounders Hardik Pandya and Nitish Kumar Reddy are on track as of now, while Washington Sundar is nearing the necessary clearances for the fixtures starting September 13 in Delhi. It is reliably learnt that Reddy has been training intensely at the BCCI Centre of Excellence (CoE) and operating at full capacity in order to return to international cricket.As for Washington Sundar, he spent the weekend in Chennai and will report back to the CoE this week to prove his fitness before selection. The men's senior selection committee chaired by Ajit Agarkar is likely to meet this week to pick the squad for the three T20Is."The practical target is the T20Is against Afghanistan and this will allow Washington Sundar to ease back into the set-up with the shortest format. His workload has gradually increased in the last few weeks, and he could be available for selection for the three T20Is," says a source tracking developments."Both Reddy and Pandya have been at the CoE for a very long time now and only take breaks for personal commitments. Reddy only goes back home during the weekends while Pandya has anyway moved base to Bengaluru," adds the source.All eyes, however, are on Jasprit Bumrah. The fast bowler missed the two Tests against Sri Lanka earlier this month and the management wants to handle him very carefully with an eye on the two Tests against New Zealand later this year. The 32-year-old has been training at the CoE. While the Afghanistan T20Is could be touch-and-go, the Asian Games shouldn't face any availability issues if there are no late hiccups during his rehabilitation."Bumrah is progressing well. In buildup to the 2027 World Cup, the plan was that he would focus on ODIs and Tests but since the knee injury, the management wants to ease him back with the shortest format first. He is being closely monitored and while the Afghanistan T20Is could be too close for comfort, the Asian Games seem highly likely, provided there are no late surprises," explains the source.Krunal Pandya back in the mix?After the recent outings in Ireland and England, the Indian team management is exploring options of left-arm spinners in the shortest format. Axar Patel played all seven games and had mediocre returns: two wickets in four T20Is against England and two wickets in two T20Is against Ireland. Krunal Pandya is being discussed, and his return to the T20I squad would not be a surprise.Krunal, who last played for India in 2021 T20 series against Sri Lanka, has been very impressive in the IPL and picked up 14 wickets for the Royal Challengers Bengaluru in the 2026 edition. It now remains to be seen whether the selectors revert to a proven performer as they look to find the right candidate for the crucial left-arm spinner spot.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'I felt sorry for the guy': Eight years later, Faf du Plessis revisits one of cricket’s darkest chapters; 'Sandpaper Gate', and believes Australia handled the scandal poorly
articles.summary: Cricket News: Eight years after the Sandpaper Gate scandal shook Australian cricket, former South Africa captain Faf du Plessis has offered a different perspective .
articles.body: Eight years after the Sandpaper Gate scandal shook Australian cricket, former South Africa captain Faf du Plessis has offered a different perspective on one of the most controversial episodes in the sport.Cameron Bancroft was caught on camera using sandpaper to alter the ball during the 2018 Cape Town Test against South Africa, setting off a scandal that engulfed the Australian team. Steve Smith and David Warner were also punished, with all three players losing their leadership positions or facing lengthy suspensions.But du Plessis believes Bancroft, in particular, was subjected to an unnecessarily harsh media trial. Speaking to former South Africa pacer Vernon Philander on the ‘Beyond the Boundary’ podcast, he said his immediate reaction was sympathy for the young Australian batter.“Bancroft, and honestly, my first instincts with him were, I felt sorry for the guy. When I saw him, first of all, he did that, and I was like, ‘Shame.’ He doesn't know what to do. He doesn't know how to get the ball to reverse swing, because taking a piece of sandpaper out of your pocket with cameras, it's not the most clever thing to do,” Faf said.The incident quickly escalated beyond the field. Du Plessis recalled how the South African team waited for Australia's press conference following the day's play, only to see the situation become even more explosive after the Australian team's statement.“Then it was that whole incident. I mean, we were sitting after the day's play. And we were like, the team is taking like an hour before the press conference has to start. So we're like, why are they taking so long? What are they doing? And then they issued that statement. And that statement was just like putting blitz under a fire and just going there. And they were saying, no one knows about it. The captain had no idea. The coach had no idea. And everyone was just like, well, hang on, what's going on here? Everyone knows what goes on in a dressing room,” he added.Du Plessis questions Australia’s responseThe scandal eventually saw Smith and Warner handed 12-month bans, while Bancroft was suspended for nine months. Smith and Warner were also removed from their leadership positions.Du Plessis believes Cricket Australia made the situation considerably bigger by allowing outside pressure, including political intervention, to influence its response.“So I think it was more the way that they handled that that caused a lot of noise. And then it went back to Australia, where the Australian Prime Minister got involved. The ex-cricketers were smashing the team about how you can do that? And we were sitting there going, come on, guys. It's not like you guys got a first to do it. You never did it. Like, don't be glasshouse,” said Faf.He also recalled reaching out to Smith during the fallout because he expected the punishment to last weeks or perhaps a month, rather than an entire year.“Everyone has done it at some stage in their career. Warner, Smith and Bancroft were the three guys who were actually caught. I felt the right thing to do was to send Steve Smith a message and say, Listen, I know you guys are trying to do the right thing. You're going to go through some crap over the next week. I thought it would be like a week or a month. But it ended up being a year. I was just like, I'm sorry you're going through this. You shouldn't take the brunt of this. It's a thing that, unfortunately, should fall on the whole team. But yeah, I felt for Bancroft. I felt sorry for him because he just didn't know how to do it. And Steve Smith for trying to do the right thing to be the captain and say, it's my show,” he added.Faf says bans were unnecessaryDu Plessis went further, arguing that the players should not have been removed from international cricket for such long periods.In his view, the International Cricket Council should have handled the disciplinary side of the incident, while Cricket Australia could have imposed financial penalties instead of lengthy bans.“I think they could have handled that a little bit better. Cricket Australia had other ideas. And they made that thing become a very big thing. Just let the ICC deal with it. I think when you let politics and stuff come into sport, it never ends well. And that's the case with the Prime Minister's politics and everyone putting pressure on them. And they're feeling like they have to act. They have to act to show that they're doing something. I think that becomes a dangerous precedent,” said Faf.Du Plessis suggested that the punishment could instead have been limited to match-fee deductions, allowing the players to continue their careers without missing an entire year.“I think if they took it on the chin on that night and said, Cameron would have said, I'm sorry, I made it a bad thing. I'm young in international cricket, and I'm sorry. Which he obviously did. But I think he would have gotten a 50 per cent match fee from the ICC. Steve Smith would have played the next Test match. David Warner, they would have played the whole rest of the year. But what ended up happening is they missed a year of cricket,” he added.For du Plessis, the Sandpaper Gate scandal was therefore not only about what happened on the field, but also about how the aftermath was handled. He believes the punishment, political pressure and public reaction turned an already serious incident into a much bigger crisis for Smith, Warner and Bancroft.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Umpires' calls and different ball': Joe Root explains lean run as he chases Sachin Tendulkar’s record
articles.summary: Cricket News: Joe Root has played down concerns over his indifferent batting form this English summer, insisting his experience and record give him confidence that .
articles.body: Joe Root has played down concerns over his indifferent batting form this English summer, insisting his experience and record give him confidence that he will find a way through the difficult patch as he continues his pursuit of Sachin Tendulkar’s record Test run tally.Root, who is chasing Tendulkar’s record of 15,921 Test runs, has crossed 50 only twice this home summer and is averaging 29.44. It is his second-lowest home season average since making his international debut 14 years ago.The 35-year-old has also been dismissed LBW nine times in his last seven Tests, including seven times this summer. Root, however, believes the conditions have made batting unusually difficult across the board.Root points to testing conditions“I've played this game a long time and I've always found ways of solving those problems and working it through,” Root told the BBC after the Lord's Test against Pakistan.“I don't see this as being any different. There's a reason why I've got 14,000 runs (14,208) and a reason why I've played the best part of 15 years at this level.“Of course it's frustrating that there's sort of a trend. There are probably four umpires' calls within that, which could have gone the other way, and the ball is probably deviating more than it ever has.”Root also pointed towards the Dukes ball as one possible reason for the unusually testing conditions faced by batters this summer. He suggested there had been a noticeable difference from last season, when England and India pushed for ball changes multiple times during their series.“The balls have been different this summer,” he said. “I think there is a different lacquer. They were worried about it going out of shape. They are denting surfaces more.”Despite his lean run, Root remains confident that he can find a solution.“You try and be realistic and understand where everything's at, but also be aware of what you need to do to keep improving and keep getting better. I'm pretty sure I'll get through the other side. I'm not too concerned about that.”‘You’re never given anything in this game’Root’s pursuit of Tendulkar’s record has brought his run-scoring under greater scrutiny, but the England batter used his current struggles to underline just how difficult sustained success in Test cricket can be.“You're never given anything in this game,” said Root. “You have to work for everything. You have to keep working hard and I'll certainly keep doing that.“You're constantly going to get challenged and you're constantly going to have to look to evolve and learn, but that's never been something I've shied away from and I certainly won't be doing moving forward.”Root’s batting struggles have not prevented England from making a strong start to his second stint as captain. England beat Pakistan by 194 runs at Lord’s to seal the series, giving Root two wins from two Tests since returning to the leadership role and England their first Test series win since 2024.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Everyone is worried’: Pakistan languish at WTC bottom after another heavy defeat
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan’s Test crisis deepened at Lord’s as another heavy away defeat left them languishing at the bottom of the World Test Championship standings, w.
articles.body: Pakistan’s Test crisis deepened at Lord’s as another heavy away defeat left them languishing at the bottom of the World Test Championship standings, with pacer Mohammad Abbas admitting that “everyone is worried” about the team’s performances.Pakistan’s fortunes in the longest format have declined significantly in recent years, both at home and overseas.Their latest setback was a 194-run defeat to England at Lord’s, following an innings defeat in the series opener at Leeds. It was Pakistan’s 10th loss in their last 11 away Tests.‘Our performance is a concern for everyone’Abbas, who finished the Lord’s Test with nine wickets and claimed his first five-wicket haul at the venue, acknowledged that Pakistan are fully aware of the problems facing them.“Our performance is a concern for everyone. Everyone is worried, including selection committee and the NCA. We're not doing well, we accept that. We're not batting, bowling or fielding well and we discuss this all the time in meetings. We're all working on it, and we need to be, too,” Abbas said after the Lord’s defeat.The pacer singled out Pakistan’s fielding as one area that needs considerable improvement. Dropped catches proved costly as England’s key batters were allowed to add significantly to their total.“We dropped catches, and their key players scored 70-odd extra runs. That's where the match changed because we could have bowled them out for 200. It's disappointing,” Abbas said.Despite his own impressive showing, the veteran pacer remained frustrated that his individual performances have not translated into victories.“Individual performances are important, but I try to perform to help the team win. It's been many matches that I've been performing, but the team hasn't won,” he said.‘Experience is very important in Test cricket’Abbas also pointed to the relative inexperience of Pakistan’s current pace attack as another challenge.“In Bangladesh, we had a different bowling combination to here. We won a Test in the West Indies. The guys are adjusting, but experience is very important in Test cricket,” he said.Abbas, who has played 32 Tests, said the younger fast bowlers alongside him are still adapting to the demands of international cricket across different conditions.“I've played 32 Test matches, but the fast bowlers playing with me are very new to Test cricket. But everybody is trying to improve.”Pakistan now have one more opportunity to avoid a series whitewash and collect valuable WTC points when they face England in the third Test at Edgbaston, beginning September 9.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: South Zone vs North Zone: Tilak, Shreyas turn the tide with marathon stand in Duleep Trophy
articles.summary: Cricket News: In the longer format, patience and discipline are traditional routes to building an innings. The beauty lies in embracing that challenge when the situ.
articles.body: In the longer format, patience and discipline are traditional routes to building an innings. The beauty lies in embracing that challenge when the situation demands it.South Zone found themselves in a similar situation on Monday. At 80/5, they were staring at the prospect of conceding first-innings lead to North Zone, who had posted 195 in their Duleep Trophy semifinal at the BCCI Centre of Excellence here.What followed over the next 271 minutes was an exhibition of restraint and disciplined batsmanship as Tilak Varma (106 batting, 225b, 7x4) and Shreyas Gopal (87, 169b, 11x4) took centre stage with a 175-run sixth-wicket partnership. Their stand eventually turned the tide, helping South secure a first-innings lead. They were 285/9 at stumps, 90 runs ahead on the second day.South, who resumed on 40/2, were rocked by the brilliance of pacer Gurnoor Brar (4/70), who arrived in the city from the Sri Lanka tour on Friday. Making the most of windy conditions, Brar produced a peach in his fifth delivery of the day to disturb Narayan Jagadeesan’s stumps. He struck again soon after, producing a similar delivery to castle R Smaran’s off stump before dismissing Kodimela Himateja for a duck.With their backs against the wall, Tilak and Shreyas joined hands and tested the North bowlers’ patience.The Karnataka all-rounder brought up his first four off the 42nd ball he faced. Tilak did not find the boundary again until his 154th delivery, with that four taking South into the lead. Having curbed his instincts and reached his fifty without a boundary, the Hyderabad batter gradually shifted gears.Shreyas, meanwhile, completed his fifty in 107 balls and looked in control as he appeared on course for his seventh first-class hundred. But pacer Arshdeep Singh ended his vigil when he edged one through to stand-in wicketkeeper Abdul Samad.With South’s tail beginning to crumble, Tilak was in danger of missing out on a deserved century. The Hyderabad batter, though, held his nerve, smashing two successive fours off Gurnoor to bring up his eighth first-class hundred in 219 balls.Interestingly, all seven of Tilak’s fours came after he reached his fifty — a reflection of the restraint that underpinned his innings. With South nine down, he will be eager to carry that momentum into the third day and stretch their lead into three figures and beyond.Brief scores: North Zone 195 vs South Zone 285/9 in 94 overs (o/n: 40/2) (Narayan Jagadeesan 36, Tilak Varma 106 batting, Shreyas Gopal 87; Arshdeep Singh 2-59, Anshul Kamboj 2-53, Gurnoor Brar 4-70).Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi makes a statement! Teenager misses ton as East Zone match Central Zone’s first-innings total
articles.summary: Cricket News: BENGALURU: In 118 minutes and 81 balls, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi offered a glimpse of the raw talent that has made him one of Indian cricket’s most sought.
articles.body: BENGALURU: In 118 minutes and 81 balls, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi offered a glimpse of the raw talent that has made him one of Indian cricket’s most sought-after prospects. The southpaw backs his big-hitting ability irrespective of the format and his fearless approach was on full display as the East Zone opener smashed 92 (7x4, 7x6) against Central Zone on Day 2 of their Duleep Trophy semifinal at the BCCI Centre of Excellence here on Monday.At 15 years and 157 days, Sooryavanshi became the youngest player to score a 50 in the tournament, breaking Central Zone’s Laxman Singh’s record of 16 years and 23 days, set in January 1969.The innings was more than just a record. Since his Ranji Trophy debut in 2024, the teenager had managed 215 runs from nine first-class matches. While he has built strong credentials in white-ball cricket, the longer format remains a stern test. Sooryavanshi was in no mood to let a red-ball challenge pass without making a statement.The first session was all about his attacking display. After getting off the mark with a risky single, the left-hander struck his first boundary with a stylish square drive. That was merely an appetiser, as he repeatedly looked to score in the V against the pacers, including Yash Thakur, whom he deposited over the bowler’s head for his first six. His 18 singles were as much a sign of maturity as his seven sixes were of his power.His domination helped East Zone race to 64 in the first 10 overs. On 40, Sooryavanshi was handed a reprieve when Yash Rathod dropped a straightforward catch off Saransh Jain. The batter made the most of it, bringing up his half-century off 42 balls with a six over long-on.What stood out was not just the power, but the range. One particular assault on pacer Aryan Pandey was striking. Charging down the track, Sooryavanshi smashed the ball straight back over the bowler’s head for his fourth six.Such was his command that it seemed to matter little who was bowling. Off-spinner Saransh Jain, who recently made his India Test debut, was dealt with equal confidence, conceding a four and a six as Sooryavanshi raced towards the nervous nineties in the 25th over.However, he was left distraught when another attempt at a maximum landed in Arshad Khan’s hands at deep mid-wicket off Harsh Dubey, leaving him eight runs short of his maiden first-class hundred.Along with Abhimanyu Easwaran’s 69, Sooryavanshi’s 92 formed the backbone of a 161-run opening stand that helped East Zone reach 266, exactly matching Central Zone’s first-innings total. Central were 45/3 at stumps.Brief scores: Central Zone 266 & 45/3 in 20 overs (Mukesh Kumar 2-14) vs East Zone 266 all out in 57 overs (Abhimanyu Easwaran 69, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi 92; Aryan Pandey 3-43, Yash Thakur 3-66, Harsh Dubey 4-66).Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Lord's pitch: MCC outlines action plan after England vs Pakistan Test to address criticism of playing surface
articles.summary: Lord's pitch was rated 'unsatisfactory' and given demerit point after second-shortest Test match in ground's history earlier this summer; watch the third Test between England and Pakistan, at Edgbaston, live on Sky Sports from Wednesday, September 9
articles.body:
Lord's was handed one demerit point under the ICC's Pitch and Outfield Monitoring Process after the staging of its 150th Test match between England and New Zealand earlier this summer proved to be the ground's second-shortest on record at 165 overs and two-and-a-half days' action.

The playing surface was back under the spotlight this week, with stats showing that there was actually more movement on offer for bowlers during England's 194-run victory over Pakistan than in the prior Test against New Zealand.

"'Unsatisfactory' was how this pitch was rated after the New Zealand Test match. I have to say, after three days of this Test match, it is 'unsatisfactory' again," Sky Sports Cricket 's Nasser Hussain said ahead of the match's conclusion on Sunday, day four of the Test.

"For two days, I thought it did less than that New Zealand game. But yesterday, because of the cloud cover, drizzle and lights being on, this pitch misbehaved.

"If you compare the stats from the New Zealand game to this one, the movement during the New Zealand game was around 0.7 degrees. Including yesterday [Saturday], it went up to 0.85 degrees for this Test.

"In the history of having these stats, that's the most movement we have ever seen in any pitch in the UK."

How is MCC taking action over Lord's pitch?

MCC ground staff worked hard in the off-season to try and bring the pitch up to Test standard, relaying the outfield and even blowing 200°C steam on the wicket, in a bid to kill pathogens in the soil.

They had hoped the measures would revitalise the ageing wicket, but the MCC has now released a new action plan in the hope of addressing concerns, which includes the introduction of drop-in pitches.

Former England and Middlesex cricketer Eoin Morgan detailed the plans further, telling Sky Sports Cricket : "It's something the MCC and Lord's take very seriously.

"The ground has taken a reputational blow when it comes to Test cricket this year. It is not two isolated events, either. When it comes to red-ball cricket, things become very challenging.

"The MCC has taken on all of the feedback following the New Zealand Test. They have put together an action plan in which there are a number of steps to try and improve things going forward.

"The MCC is committed to investing financially in getting informed analysis to make this better. There's pitch relaying which will be staged on the TV pitches and permanent drop-in pitches that will be prepared on the Nursery Ground.

"This will give the MCC the ability to identify certain match pitches that can be preserved and used for specific games.

"We had 63 days of cricket here this year. The MCC has engaged with a partner at Wormsley to manage the lead-in to match days.

"We need to get this right because the consequence of how your pitch plays, and how you put on big match days, has resulted in the World Test Championship final being awarded to The Oval.

"That brought with it a little bit of baggage."

Any blame for the extravagant movement on offer at Lord's during the Pakistan Test match can't solely be laid at the pitch's door, however.

Batting was at its toughest on day three - Emilio Gay's dismissal being a particularly eye-catching one when pinned lbw by an extremely low-bouncing ball from Mohammad Abbas - as the cloud cover overhead on a rain-affected afternoon certainly played its part.

"Why is it moving so much?" Hussain added. "The pitch started soft and the Dukes ball makes indentations and marks on the pitch.

"Add in the slope and the overhead conditions and that makes it an absolute nightmare for the batters."

Speaking after England's series-clinching victory, Test captain Joe Root also mentioned the Dukes ball as part of the issue.

"I know The Home of Cricket is desperate to produce the best surface possible and I'm sure they're doing everything they can to provide that moving forward," Root said.

"I think the balls have been very different this year. I think there's a different lacquer on them, I've not got evidence on that and probably need to ask Dukes, but I think there's a lacquer on the seam. They don't want them to go out of shape.

"I think that they are affecting the wickets; they're dinting more and, as a batter, when you practise, they're cracking your bats more frequently.

"They seem a lot firmer and probably if they're dinting the wickets, then it's going to seam off the dints as well."

articles.title: England vs Ireland: Alice Capsey on her confidence keeping for the second time in her career
articles.summary: Alice Capsey will keep wicket for England this week despite having only done it once in her career, but remains confident of successfully doing the job.
articles.body:
When England gathered for their pre-series photo shoot on Monday, Alice Capsey had to remember an extra piece of kit.

Capsey has batted and bowled for her country. She has also grown to be one of their most reliable fielders and is talked of as a future leader aged 22.

But she also needed her wicketkeeping gloves because in this week's one-day international series against Ireland, she will be England's keeper, despite having only done the job once in a professional match - a 50-over game for South East Stars in 2020.

"Realistically, it is a bit of an unknown," Capsey tells BBC Sport. "In games, I have not done it a huge amount.

"But the work I have done off the pitch, I know I am putting a lot of hard work in. It gives me a lot of confidence."

In truth, this is not a punt in the dark. Coach Charlotte Edwards is not fond of those.

England first discussed having Capsey, who was a wicketkeeper for much of her junior career, as an option during their pre-season camp in South Africa earlier this year.

Amid a dearth of alternatives and after some early-season work, the 22-year-old was listed as the back-up to regular keeper Amy Jones for this summer's T20 World Cup.

She was never needed but when captain Nat Sciver-Brunt returned from injury for England's semi-final, the idea of in-form batter Sophia Dunkley keeping her place, Jones missing out and Capsey taking the gloves was on the table before ultimately being dismissed.

"Especially at the beginning of the summer, I was pretty nervous to do it," Capsey says.

"I went into my shell a little bit and was quite internal. It was awesome to have Sophie Ecclestone and those characters who are outgoing, jokey and keep everything relaxed.

"Everyone has seen me train so much now over the course of the summer it is second nature."

Like all good keepers, Capsey loves the rough and tumble that comes with the job.

"The amount of times you take blows on the fingers, or one goes down the leg side and you miss it..." she says.

"But those are the bits you enjoy, working to get better and better."

Capsey was a keeper when she came through the Surrey academy, only putting down her gloves when she started playing for a higher age group short of an off-spinner.

"Who knows if I hadn't played up whether I would have just kept on keeping, but it is really cool going back to the roots and where I started," she says.

England 'just humans' as Ireland target ODI upset

Her time at Bede's School in Sussex also coincided with that of former England wicketkeeper Sarah Taylor, who worked there as a sports coach before moving back into the professional game where she now works with England's men.

It gave Capsey - a 12-year-old spectator in the stands when Taylor and England won the 2017 World Cup at Lord's - the chance to work with her wicketkeeping hero who is regarded as one of the best keepers the world has seen.

"The way she went about it, did it her way and brought an X-factor to it was really cool," Capsey says.

"She has been on my shoulder for the last four or five years saying I need to get back to keeping.

"It has been awesome to touch base with her, especially this summer to be able to message her and say 'I am back'."

Capsey began ramping up her glovework in training at the start of the summer, fitting drills around her batting, bowling and out-fielding.

She has also had to tweak her sessions in the gym to strengthen her legs and, in particular, her abductors for those squats behind the stumps.

"I have pulled up, touch wood, after all of it so far," Capsey says. "Come back to me at the end of the week."

And while it is six years since her last official outing, Capsey did keep behind closed doors in one of England's warm-ups against India before the T20 World Cup.

She took a tidy, rising catch off seamer Dani Gibson while standing up to the stumps, a stumping off spinner Linsey Smith and did not concede a bye.

"It was awesome," Capsey says. "I loved the experience.

"Keeping up to Gibbo was a really nice challenge.

"That catch was one of the highlights but also it is the little things, whether in the first over stood back to [Lauren] Filer and getting one cleanly in the hands, there were a couple of leg-side takes as well."

Capsey has also been standing up to the stumps to Issy Wong, one of England's quicker bowlers, in training this week.

The wider knock-on could be intriguing, if these three one-day internationals go well.

At the very least, it will provide a convenient back-up to 33-year-old Jones, who has been rested for this series, and some competition for places.

And, after Jones returned five single-figure scores in seven World Cup innings this year, it could free up a space for a more explosive batter in England's top order, given Capsey has already cemented her place in the team through her batting alone.

"There is going to be nerves and pressure around, but more internal pressure than anything," Capsey says.

"As a professional athlete you don't want to do it badly and you are representing England.

"It is an international series, there are ICC points on the line.

"To be trusted to have the gloves for England has got to give you confidence as well.

"I am not the finished article by any means but I did it for a long time growing up.

"Regardless of the challenges presented this week I know I have a bit of experience to fall back on which is nice."

articles.title: Women’s Asia Cup: Sobhana Mostary recalls the India win that ‘changed everything’ for Bangladesh
articles.summary: Cricket News: The 2026 Women’s Asia Cup is already underway and Bangladesh enter the tournament with a familiar opportunity - to test themselves against the best in.
articles.body: The 2026 Women’s Asia Cup is already underway and Bangladesh enter the tournament with a familiar opportunity - to test themselves against the best in Asia and, potentially, India.For Sobhana Mostary, however, the Asia Cup carries a significance that goes well beyond the matches ahead. Six years after Bangladesh’s historic triumph in 2018, the memories of that campaign remain deeply connected to how she views the tournament and the growth of women’s cricket in her country.Bangladesh women's cricket has come a long way since its historic victory over India in the 2018 Women's Asia Cup, a victory that Sobhana Mostary believes transformed the nature of the sport in her country.For Mostary, the 2018 triumph remains a defining moment for Bangladesh women's cricket.“After 2018, we beat India and won the Asia Cup, so it was a huge change in Bangladesh women's cricket. Everything changed. They started giving us lots of facilities, money, everything. There was a lot of change,” Mostary told TimesofIndia.com in an exclusive interaction ahead of the Women’s Asia Cup 2026.In their 2018 campaign, Bangladesh beat India twice in the tournament, including a seven-wicket win in the group stage, before defeating the defending champions by three wickets in a thrilling final in Kuala Lumpur to win their maiden Women's Asia Cup title. The final went down to the last ball, with Jahanara Alam completing the winning two runs as Bangladesh chased down India's 112/9.The impact was immediate. Bangladesh Cricket Board announced a Bangladeshi Taka 2 crore reward for the victorious women's team. For Mostary, the legacy of that victory remains relevant even years later.“We think this Asia Cup, we fight for the title, because if we beat India, so maybe we own the Asia Cup,” she said.Now, as Bangladesh prepare for another Asia Cup campaign, Mostary knows the challenge is different. Bangladesh are in Group B alongside Sri Lanka, Indonesia and the UAE, while India are in Group A with Pakistan, Thailand and Hong Kong. A meeting between the two sides can only come in the knockout stage.From a village academy to international cricketMostary's own journey began far away from the international spotlight. She started playing several sports as a child, including football, badminton and cricket. At the age of 10, her father took her to a cricket academy in her village. After around six months of training, she attended a trial conducted by the Bangladesh Krira Shiksha Pratisthan (BKSP) and was selected.That selection changed the course of her life. Mostary moved to Dhaka without her parents to pursue cricket. Her international debut came remarkably early. She was just 16 years old when she first played for Bangladesh.But making her debut did not immediately translate into a regular place in the XI. Mostary recalled spending the next three to three-and-a-half years travelling with the Bangladesh team without getting consistent opportunities to play.“It was very difficult. I always travelled with the team, but couldn't play. I just waited and thought that someday the opportunity would come and I could show my strength, ” she said.‘Day by day, I improve’The patience eventually began to pay off. The ICC described Mostary as a bright future prospect in 2023, but the batter believes she is still working towards fulfilling that potential.“I don't think I have fulfilled my dream and that bright future yet, but day by day, I improve, ” she said.Harmanpreet Kaur: The childhood idolInterestingly, one of Mostary's biggest inspirations comes from across the border. Her childhood idol is Harmanpreet Kaur, the India captain whose batting left a lasting impression on her as a young cricketer from Bangladesh. Mostary specifically recalled watching Harmanpreet's memorable 2017 Women's World Cup innings against Australia, when the Indian batter smashed an unbeaten 171.“That match inspired me a lot, I followed her batting, everything how she controls the match, and now the time how she captains. I just followed everything, ” Mostary admitted.Playing India, in fact, remains something she describes as exciting rather than intimidating.“For Bangladeshi fans, playing India is a very good match. They are crazy fans and lots of supporters come to watch. It is a normal match, but normally playing India is very interesting and always very exciting for us,” she added.Mostary also has a particular appreciation for India's bowling attack. Asked which Indian bowler she would like to face, she picked Deepti Sharma, praising the all-rounder's consistency and variety.“Deepti Sharma is always the top bowler in the Indian side, she has played consistently for so many years and improved day by day. I love her bowling, ” Mostary said.A session with Laura WolvaardtWhile Harmanpreet remains her childhood idol, Mostary has another player she would love to train with, South Africa captain Laura Wolvaardt.“I want to practise with Laura Wolvaardt, I really like her batting, and she's also a good human being,” she said.Cricket over medicineThere was a time when cricket was not even Mostary's first career choice. Asked what she might have done had she not pursued cricket, she revealed that becoming a doctor was a possibility.“Maybe a doctor, because my mother wanted me to be a doctor,” she said.Instead, the 16-year-old who once left home to pursue cricket has now spent years representing Bangladesh on the international stage.“I struggled for three or four years, but now I have improved,” she said.And with India once again standing in Bangladesh's path, Mostary knows exactly what another victory could mean.(Watch DP World Women's Asia live on Sony Sports Ten 1 SD & HD & Sony LIV.)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: England v Pakistan: Tourists drop seven players, call up seven and release coach Sarfaraz Ahmed
articles.summary: Pakistan respond to their series defeat by England by taking the extraordinary step of dropping seven players, calling up five uncapped players and releasing their head coach.
articles.body:
Pakistan have responded to their series defeat by England by taking the extraordinary step of dropping seven players, calling up five uncapped players and releasing their head coach.

After two one-sided defeats in the first two Tests, the tourists have revamped their squad and backroom staff for the third and final match of the series at Edgbaston.

Five of the players dropped - Muhammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq, Salman Ali Agha, Ali Usman and Khurram Shahzad - have featured in the series so far, while Aamir Jamal and Muhammad Awais Jafar have been sent home without playing.

A total of seven players have been called up. Batters Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal have previous Test experience and join the quintet of uncapped newcomers.

Spin-bowling all-rounder Arafat Minhas, left-arm seamer Mohammed Imran Jr, wicketkeeper Said Baig and all-rounders Mohammad Imran and Razaullah have all received call-ups.

In addition, head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and his assistant Umar Gul have been released to be replaced by Pakistan white-ball coach Mike Hesson and former Australia seamer Ashley Noffke.

The third Test in Birmingham begins on 9 September.

Pakistan have been abject in the opening two Tests, losing the first at Headingley by an innings and the second at Lord's by 194 runs. They have been bowled out for less than 200 in each of their four innings.

The response is remarkable. For a touring team to send home seven players and the head coach mid-series is unprecedented.

Pakistan have a history of making eccentric decisions in the wake of defeats. On England's last tour of Pakistan in 2024, the hosts responded to losing the first Test, when England made a total in excess of 800, by playing the second Test on the same pitch in Multan.

On that occasion, Pakistan used garden heaters and fans to dry the surface, to assist their spinners. The home side won the next two Tests to win the series 2-1.

Pakistan to meet King Charles after Lord's controversy

Sarfaraz denies knowing about Pakistan threat to end tour

Now, among the seven players sent home are Salman, who captained in the first Test in the absence of the injured Babar Azam, then was dropped for the second.

Also dropped is opener Imam-ul-Haq, who was criticised at Lord's for not attempting to bat in either innings after suffering a calf injury while fielding on the opening day.

The sweeping selection changes come after the Pakistan team were surrounded by controversy during the second Test.

At lunch on the first day, the Pakistan Cricket Board threatened to cancel the remainder of the match and tour because of an interview with the sons of Imran Khan that was broadcast by Sky.

Imran, the former Pakistan captain and prime minster, has been in prison for three years on charges of corruption, which he denies.

Pakistan ultimately completed the Test, with both captain Babar and head coach Sarfaraz denying any knowledge of a planned boycott.

The tourists are also due to have an audience with King Charles at Clarence House this week.

articles.title: Zimbabwe survive huge Namibia scare, clinch five-run win in final-over thriller
articles.summary: Cricket News: Zimbabwe survived a stunning late fightback from Namibia to pull off a thrilling five-run victory in Windhoek, recovering from a precarious 101/6 to p.
articles.body: Zimbabwe survived a stunning late fightback from Namibia to pull off a thrilling five-run victory in Windhoek, recovering from a precarious 101/6 to post 195/6 before holding their nerve in a dramatic final over.Namibia, who had opened the tri-series with an impressive win over South Africa, looked out of the contest at 76/6 during their chase. But Zane Green and Alexander Volschenk produced a breathtaking 109-run seventh-wicket partnership off just 49 balls to put Namibia within touching distance of another remarkable victory.Zimbabwe eventually held on, with Brad Evans delivering the decisive final over to seal a result that looked highly unlikely midway through the chase.Zimbabwe recover from 101/6Asked to bat first, Zimbabwe made an aggressive start through Ben Curran and Brian Bennett, who put on 64 for the opening wicket. Namibia struck with the final ball of the Powerplay when Bennett top-edged a pull off JJ Smit to deep midwicket for 32 off 21 balls.Dion Myers fell to Bernard Scholtz in the following over, before Gerhard Erasmus produced the biggest breakthrough by dismissing Sikandar Raza for a golden duck. Curran was then removed in the ninth over, and Erasmus struck again soon after to send back Wesley Madhavere.Zimbabwe had slumped to 79/5 in the 10th over and were in danger of being bowled out cheaply. But Ryan Burl and Brad Evans turned the innings around with a crucial 94-run partnership off 48 balls.Namibia's decision to return to spin for the final over proved particularly expensive. Burl smashed Erasmus for a six and three consecutive fours, taking 20 from the over as Zimbabwe surged to 195/6.Namibia’s stunning fightback falls agonisingly shortNamibia's chase began with early pressure from Zimbabwe. Louren Steenkamp was dismissed by Blessing Muzarabani in the third over, while Erasmus made 12 before falling to Brad Evans.Loftie-Eaton briefly counterattacked with 20 off 13, but Brian Bennett then struck twice in three balls to leave Namibia at 66/4. Frylinck's 22 off 29 was unable to halt the slide, and when Ruben Trumpelmann fell to Sikandar Raza, Namibia were reeling at 76/6.Then came the extraordinary recovery.Volschenk attacked the bowling from the outset, hitting Wellington Masakadza for two sixes in the 13th over. Green joined him, and the pair combined power with sharp running to keep Namibia's hopes alive.Their partnership raced past 100, leaving Namibia needing only 16 from the final over with four wickets still in hand.Evans began the last over with a no-ball, but Namibia could take only two runs from it. Green was then run out for 54 off 26 after being caught short at the non-striker's end by a direct hit from Raza.Volschenk kept Namibia alive with a boundary but was dismissed for 56 off 29 when he edged a full, wide delivery, with wicketkeeper Tadiwanashe Marumani taking a superb one-handed catch.With two balls remaining, Namibia needed nine. Scholtz was run out attempting a desperate single before Evans held his nerve to bowl Jack Brassell for a duck and complete Zimbabwe's five-run victory.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan have responded to their crushing 194-run defeat to England at Lord’s with a sweeping mid-tour overhaul, releasing seven players and making ch.
articles.body: Pakistan have responded to their crushing 194-run defeat to England at Lord’s with a sweeping mid-tour overhaul, releasing seven players and making changes to the red-ball coaching staff ahead of the third Test at Edgbaston.The Pakistan Cricket Board announced the changes on Monday after Pakistan slipped to a 0-2 deficit in the three-match series. The defeat at Lord’s followed an innings-and-103-run loss in Leeds, leaving Pakistan with five defeats in their last six Tests.Among the seven players released are former white-ball captain Salman Ali Agha, wicketkeeper-batter Mohammad Rizwan and opening batter Imam-ul-Haq. Ali Usman, Aamir Jamal, Muhammad Awais Zafar and Khurram Shahzad have also been released.“The Pakistan Cricket Board has today announced that seven players have been released from the Test squad following completion of the Lord’s Test. A total of seven replacements have been named including five uncapped players at Test level and two capped players,” the PCB said in its statement.Saim Ayub, Abdullah Fazal among replacementsThe board has brought in seven replacements, including Test-capped batters Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal, along with left-arm spin-bowling all-rounder Arafat Minhas.Saim has played eight Tests for Pakistan, while Abdullah has featured in two. Minhas has represented Pakistan in three ODIs and four T20Is.“Among the players announced as replacements, batters Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal have played eight and two Tests, respectively, while left-arm spin-bowling all-rounder Arafat Minhas has represented Pakistan in three ODIs and four T20Is,” the PCB said.Four uncapped players at Test level have also been added to the squad — left-arm fast bowler Mohammad Imran Jnr, wicketkeeper-batter Saad Baig, and right-arm pace-bowling all-rounders Mohammad Imran, also known as Imran Randhawa, and Razaullah.“The four other players are left-arm fast bowler Mohammad Imran Jnr, wicketkeeper-batter and player of the tournament of Quaid-e-Azam Trophy 2025-26 Saad Baig, right-arm pace bowling all-rounders Mohammad Imran (also known as Imran Randhawa) and Razaullah,” the PCB added.Sarfaraz Ahmed, Umar Gul also releasedThe changes extend beyond the playing squad, with red-ball head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul also relieved of their duties.White-ball head coach Mike Hesson and Ashley Noffke will take over the backroom responsibilities for the remainder of the England tour.“Additionally, Sarfaraz Ahmed and Umar Gul have also been released and will be replaced by Mike Hesson and Ashley Noffke in the backroom staff,” the PCB said.The overhaul follows growing scrutiny of several players after the Lord’s defeat. Imam came under criticism after missing both innings because of a calf injury sustained on the opening day. His appearance on the outfield for warm-ups on the fourth morning drew further attention.Rizwan’s position had also come under pressure after another difficult outing with the bat. His dismissal in the second innings, when he was trapped lbw attempting a slog, added to questions over his place.Pakistan will now attempt to salvage something from the series when they face England in the third Test at Edgbaston from September 9.Updated Pakistan Test squad for Birmingham Test: Babar Azam (captain), Abdullah Fazal, Arafat Minhas, Azan Awais, Mohammad Abbas, Mohammad Ali, Muhammad Imran, Mohammad Imran Jnr, Muhammad Ghazi Ghori (wicket-keeper), Razaullah, Saad Baig (wicket-keeper), Saim Ayub, Sajid Khan, Saud Shakeel, Shan Masood and Ubaid ShahGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Scotland beat Netherlands by nine wickets to level ODI series
articles.summary: Scotland level their one-day international series with the Netherlands at 1-1 after a thumping nine-wicket victory in a rain-affected match in Stirling.
articles.body:
Netherlands 129-9 (32 overs): De Leede 58; Maqsood 3-20, Carter 2-18

Scotland 130-1 (16.2 overs): S Bryce 70*, Carter 33*

Scotland levelled their one-day international series with the Netherlands at 1-1 after a thumping nine-wicket victory in a rain-affected match in Stirling.

Sarah Bryce, captaining the side in the absence of her sister Kathyrn, led the way with an unbeaten 70 as the hosts chased down their target of 130 in just over half of their allotted 32 overs, in a game which was originally scheduled for Sunday but fell foul of the weather.

The Dutch had enjoyed a 58-run win in Glasgow on Friday and this was another one-sided contest.

Darcy Carter made an early breakthrough, taking the wickets of Netherlands openers Phebe Molkenboer and Sanya Khurana, who had piled on more than 150 in last week's encounter.

Abtaha Maqsood also took two quick wickets to leave the visitors reeling on 39-4.

Maqsood struck again but Babette de Leede made 58 before being run out, while Caroline de Lange added 20 on the way to their total of 129-9.

Scotland lost Maryam Faisal after four balls but Carter (33 not out) and Bryce made sure of a comprehensive success.

Wicketkeeper Bryce, who took two catches, settled the match with her 11th four, while the Dutch bowlers sent down 17 wides in 16 overs.

While it may have been a bruising defeat, the visitors do have cause for celebration since the completed match was enough to regain their ODI ranking and avoid a significant drop in funding.

The teams will meet again on Tuesday at the same venue to decide the series.

articles.title: ‘Not a good decision’: Ex-Pakistan cricketer fumes at PCB, sends message to Mohsin Naqvi
articles.summary: Cricket News: Former Pakistan cricketer Kamran Akmal has criticised the Pakistan Cricket Board's decision to release seven players from the squad midway through the.
articles.body: Former Pakistan cricketer Kamran Akmal has criticised the Pakistan Cricket Board's decision to release seven players from the squad midway through the England Test series, arguing that the move could have a damaging impact on the remaining members of the team.The PCB confirmed on Monday evening that Mohammad Rizwan, Salman Ali Agha and Imam-ul-Haq were among the seven players sent back to Pakistan after the team's disappointing results in the first two Tests against England.The board also announced seven replacements ahead of the third and final Test in Birmingham. In another major shake-up, Test head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul were released from their roles, with white-ball coaches Mike Hesson and Ashley Noffke taking over.Akmal questioned the need to send senior players home when they could simply have been left out of the playing XI.“There was one more Test left. You could have had both Agha and Rizwan in the squad. You could have dropped them from the playing XI. You should have kept them in the squad. They are your senior players. They have been captains. Sending them back is not a good message for the remaining players,” Akmal said on the ‘Game Plan’ show.The former wicketkeeper-batter believes the decision could increase the pressure on those still in the squad, particularly with Pakistan already struggling during the series.“This will result in more pressure for the remainder of the team. It is not a good decision; if you are sending them back, then the chairman, Mohsin Naqvi, needs to rejig the entire system. Make a new team. This decision to send back players is not good for our country, and it doesn't send a good message to the rest of the world,” he added.Agha's situation has also raised questions over the timing of the decision. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Hardik Pandya's return to international cricket is poised to face another roadblock, as a late leg niggle derailed his plans at the BCCI Centre of Excellence (CoE) and puts the all-rounder on the back foot for the three-match T20I series against Afghanistan.TimesofIndia.com reliably learnt that he was ticking the right boxes but the late development could well make him unavailable for selection. The selectors are expected to meet this week to pick the squad for the T20Is starting September 13 in New Delhi and will be soon briefed on the fitness status of players recovering in Bengaluru."Hardik Pandya was operating at full intensity without any discomfort but he has been advised to pause bowling due to discomfort in the leg. He will resume soon, but the Afghanistan series is too close to reach the required fitness levels. Batting and movement-wise, there wasn't any significant issue, but the CoE needs to be completely convinced before giving an all-clear," says a source tracking developments.The 32-year-old has not played a competitive fixture since turning out for Mumbai Indians in the IPL on May 24. Additionally, his last appearance for Men in Blue came on March 8 in the T20 World Cup final. Ever since, he has missed the white-ball assignments at home against Afghanistan and the subsequent tours of Ireland and England. The latest development has further delayed his return to international cricket.It is worth pointing out that Pandya had suffered a late relapse before the ODI series against Afghanistan with a low-grade quadriceps sprain. Even then, he had been at peak fitness and training well before the injury struck.As reported on Monday, all-rounders Nitish Kumar Reddy and Washington Sundar are progressing well for the Afghanistan series but Jasprit Bumrah remains touch-and-go for those three fixtures. articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi smashes 92, becomes youngest batter to hit Duleep Trophy fifty
articles.summary: Cricket News: Bengaluru: In 118 minutes and 81 balls, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi offered a glimpse of the raw talent that has made him one of Indian cricket’s most sought.
articles.body: Bengaluru: In 118 minutes and 81 balls, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi offered a glimpse of the raw talent that has made him one of Indian cricket’s most sought-after prospects. The southpaw backs his big-hitting ability irrespective of the format and his fearless approach was on full display as the East Zone opener smashed 92 (7x4, 7x6) against Central Zone on Day 2 of their Duleep Trophy semifinal at the BCCI Centre of Excellence here on Monday.At 15 years and 157 days, Sooryavanshi became the youngest player to score a 50 in the tournament, breaking Central Zone’s Laxman Singh’s record of 16 years and 23 days, set way back in Jan 1969.The innings was more than just a record. Since his Ranji Trophy debut in 2024, the teenager had managed 215 runs from nine first-class matches. While he has built strong credentials in white-ball cricket, the longer format remains a stern test. Sooryavanshi was in no mood to let a red-ball challenge pass without making a statement.The first session was all about his attacking display. After getting off the mark with a risky single, the left-hander struck his first boundary with a stylish square drive. That was merely an appetiser, as he repeatedly looked to score in the ‘V’ against the pacers, including Yash Thakur, whom he deposited over the bowler’s head for his first six. His 18 singles were as much a sign of maturity as his seven sixes were of his power. His domination helped East Zone race to 64 in the first 10 overs. On 40, Sooryavanshi was handed a reprieve when Yash Rathod dropped a straightforward catch off Saransh Jain. The batter made the most of it, bringing up his half-century off 42 balls with a six over long-on.However, he was left distraught when another attempt at a maximum landed in Arshad Khan’s hands at deep mid-wicket off Harsh Dubey, leaving him eight runs short of his maiden first-class hundred. Along with Abhimanyu Easwaran’s 69, Sooryavanshi’s 92 formed the backbone of a 161-run opening stand that helped East Zone reach 266, exactly matching Central Zone’s first-innings total. Central were 45/3 at stumps.Tilak hits patient tonIn the longer format, patience and discipline are traditional routes to building an innings. The beauty lies in embracing that challenge when the situation demands it.South Zone found themselves in that situation. At 80/5, they were staring at the prospect of conceding a first-innings lead to North Zone, who had posted 195. What followed over the next 271 minutes was an exhibition of restraint and disciplined batsmanship as Tilak Varma (106 batting, 225b, 7x4) and Shreyas Gopal (87, 169b, 11x4) took centre stage with a 175-run sixth-wicket partnership.Their stand turned the tide, helping South secure a first-innings lead. They were 285/9 at stumps, 90 ahead.Brief scores: Central Zone 266 & 45/3 (M Kumar 2-14) vs East Zone 266 all out ( V Sooryavanshi 92, A Easwaran 69; H Dubey 4-66); North Zone 195 vs South Zone 285/9 in 94 overs (o/n: 40/2) (Ti Varma 106*, S Gopal 87; G Brar 4-70).Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Siddhesh Lad to replace Shardul Thakur as Mumbai captain for 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season
articles.summary: Cricket News: Mumbai: Mumbai will have a new captain for the second successive Ranji Trophy season, with seasoned batter Siddhesh Lad set to take charge of the 42-t.
articles.body: Mumbai: Mumbai will have a new captain for the second successive Ranji Trophy season, with seasoned batter Siddhesh Lad set to take charge of the 42-time champions in the 2026-27 campaign. Lad will replace allrounder Shardul Thakur, who led Mumbai across formats during the previous domestic season.Confirming the development, Mumbai senior selection committee chairman Rajesh Pawar said the decision was taken keeping both leadership continuity and workload management in mind.“Yes, we’ve decided to appoint Siddhesh as our captain for the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season. He did well last season and is experienced. Shardul is our match-winner. There is already too much workload on him as he’s expected to bowl a lot of overs, take wickets and contribute with the bat as well. We don’t want to burden him with the responsibility of captaincy. Plus, we’ll have to manage his workload. There are 10 games in the Ranji Trophy and he may have to rest for the odd match,” Pawar told TOI on Monday.Pawar said both players had been consulted before the move was finalised.“We’ve spoken to both Siddhesh and Shardul about it, and both are positive about it. Since the season starts with four Ranji Trophy matches in October, we wanted clarity on the captaincy well in advance,” he added.The appointment rewards a stellar domestic season from Lad, who was Mumbai’s standout performer with the bat in the 2025-26 Ranji Trophy. The 34-year-old amassed 774 runs in eight matches at an impressive average of 77.40, striking five centuries to finish as the team’s leading run-scorer.Over the course of an accomplished first-class career, Lad has compiled 5,623 runs in 82 matches at 44.27, including 15 hundreds and 30 fifties. Mumbai begin their Ranji Trophy season against Chandigarh at Wankhede Stadium from Oct 11-14. They are placed in Elite Group D alongside Chandigarh, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Railways, Tamil Nadu and Uttarakhand. Mumbai last lifted the Ranji Trophy in 2023-2024 under Ajinkya Rahane.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'T20 players included for Tests': Shahid Afridi, Shoaib Malik slam Pakistan selectors over squad selection amid chaos in England tour
articles.summary: Shahid Afridi slammed Pakistan selectors over bizarre squad changes and the sacking of coach Sarfaraz midway through the England tour.
articles.body:
Shahid Afridi criticised PCB for including T20 specialists in Pakistan's Test squad ahead of the Edgbaston decider.

Afridi also questioned the decision to sack head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed after just five Test matches in charge.

Seven players were released overall, with only two experienced additions among the new faces brought into the squad.

Shoaib Malik labelled PCB's decision 'ridiculous'.

Shahid Afridi tears into Pakistan selectors for picking T20 players to resolve England test crisis

Shahid Afridi has added his voice to the growing backlash against the Pakistan Cricket Board, questioning why T20 specialists were suddenly drafted into a Test squad and why the head coach lost his job just five matches into the role.

The Pakistan think tank acted indecisively after a 194-run defeat at Lord's, which handed England an unassailable 2-0 series lead and effectively turned the final Test at Edgbaston into a dead rubber.

In the aftermath of the defeat, the PCB tore up both the playing squad and the coaching staff ahead of that last match. Seven players were released in total, five of whom had featured in the series: Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq, Salman Ali Agha, Ali Usman and Khurram Shahzad, whereas Aamir Jamal and Muhammad Awais Zafar were the casualties despite not making an appearance on the tour.

The coaching shake-up matched the scale of the playing changes. Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul were both relieved of their duties, with white-ball head coach Mike Hesson and former Australia seamer Ashley Noffke stepping in.

Among the replacements, only Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal carry any real Test experience, having played eight and two Tests respectively. The rest of the new additions are uncapped.

Spin-bowling all-rounder Arafat Minhas, left-arm seamer Mohammad Imran Jnr, wicketkeeper Saad Baig, and pace-bowling all-rounders Mohammad Imran and Razaullah round out the group.

What did Shahid Afridi say about the squad changes?

Afridi took to X to voice his confusion over the entire decision-making process, particularly the choice to bring in players better known for their T20 background into a red-ball fixture.

"Not sure what is the logic or reasoning behind this decision! Even the replacements make no sense - T20 players have been included for a Test match in England? What is this thinking and approach?" Afridi wrote.

He was equally critical of sacking Sarfaraz Ahmed so early into his tenure as head coach, calling it one of the most baffling calls he'd ever seen from a selection panel. "Why has the coach been axed after 5 Test matches? This is the most shocking decision ever by a selection committee which includes so many experienced selectors."

Sarfaraz was appointed as Pakistan's red-ball head coach on April 18, taking charge just before a two-match Test tour of Bangladesh.

It was his very first assignment in the role, which ended in a 2-0 whitewash. Pakistan then travelled to the West Indies for a two-match series that finished 1-1, before arriving in England, where they now trail 2-0 with just the Edgbaston Test remaining.

Shoaib Malik calls out PCB for disrespectful gesture

Another former Pakistan all-rounder, Shoaib Malik, joined Shahid Afridi in calling out PCB's ridiculous decision of sending back seven players back to the country in the middle of a tour, as he termed it a disrespectful gesture.

On X, Malik wrote, "The players dropped from the squad are still our national cricketers who have served Pakistan. Phrases like 'sent on the first flight back' are disrespectful. Accountability should start with those who broke the system, not with players, especially those who were on the bench or have played 2-3 test matches. Plus accountability starts once a tour is done, not in the middle of it."

He added, "Players should not be going through such mental stress and social media after every bad game or the fear of failure will settle in the minds of our players."

Afridi's criticism cuts right to the heart of the problem

Afridi's frustration isn't just noise; it reflects a valid concern about squad-building logic. Selecting T20 specialists for a Test match, especially one played in English conditions that typically demand patience and technical solidity, suggests a decision driven by panic rather than any coherent red-ball strategy.

It's hard to see how players developed for short-format explosiveness are meant to suddenly adapt to five-day discipline overnight. The coaching decision is arguably even harder to defend. Five Test matches, spanning three different series and vastly different conditions, aren't nearly enough time to fairly judge whether a head coach's methods are working.

Sacking Sarfaraz this quickly sends a troubling signal to future candidates about job security within Pakistan's setup, and it does little to build any long-term coherence in how the team approaches Test cricket.

Afridi's blunt criticism might ruffle feathers within the board, but it echoes what plenty of former players and analysts have already flagged: Pakistan's Test cricket problems run far deeper than personnel, they're rooted in an approach that keeps mistaking constant change for genuine progress. Until that mindset shifts, results like this dead-rubber chaos will likely keep repeating.

articles.body: Former Pakistan batter Basit Ali has claimed that a fallout between Babar Azam and Shaheen Shah Afridi over the captaincy played a major role in the national team’s decline.Basit’s comments came after Pakistan’s miserable showing in England, where they have already surrendered the three-match Test series 2-0 following a 194-run defeat at Lord’s. The visitors have faced widespread criticism for their performances, with the team struggling to show any fight in either of the opening two Tests.According to Basit, however, Pakistan’s problems go much deeper than the current results. He believes the leadership dispute between two of the country’s senior players created a damaging divide within the setup.“Babar Azam is not a strong captain. I am not speaking about this based on the performance in England. He has made many wrong decisions. The main reason for Pakistan cricket's downfall is the rift between Shaheen and Babar. When there was a falling-out between the two over the captaincy, Pakistan cricket was ruined that day,” Ali said on the ‘Game Plan’ show.He also suggested that the consequences of the dispute are still visible in Pakistan cricket.“Many statements were made, saying Shaheen is a very good bowler and Babar is a very good bowler. The rift, whoever created that, the side effects can be seen now,” he added.Babar and Shaheen captaincy sagaPakistan’s leadership has gone through repeated changes since the 2023 ODI World Cup.Babar stepped down as captain after Pakistan’s disappointing campaign in India, with Shaheen subsequently handed the ODI leadership. However, after Pakistan’s poor results in New Zealand, Babar returned to the captaincy.His second stint did not last long either. Babar was removed again after Pakistan failed to reach the semi-finals of the 2024 T20 World Cup.The constant reshuffling has now left Pakistan with separate captains across formats. Babar leads the Test side, Shaheen is the ODI captain, while Salman Ali Agha is in charge of the T20I team.Basit believes the damage caused by the earlier captaincy dispute cannot be ignored while assessing Pakistan’s current struggles.Major changes after England disasterThe PCB has now begun making changes following the disastrous England tour.On Monday, the board decided to send seven players home, with Mohammad Rizwan and Salman Ali Agha among those affected. Test coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul were also removed from the setup.White-ball coach Mike Hesson will take charge of Pakistan for the third and final Test against England in Birmingham.While Babar remains Pakistan’s Test captain, Shaheen has not been part of the red-ball setup and is currently out of favour in Test cricket.Babar took over as Test captain from Shan Masood earlier this year. Under his leadership, Pakistan drew a two-match Test series against the West Indies.However, his own batting form in the longest format remains a concern. articles.summary: Cricket News: Former Pakistan batter and PCB chairman Ramiz Raja has criticised the current board for what he described as a panic-driven response to the team’s dis.
articles.body: Former Pakistan batter and PCB chairman Ramiz Raja has criticised the current board for what he described as a panic-driven response to the team’s disastrous Test tour of England.The PCB made sweeping changes after Pakistan lost the first two Tests of the three-match series, sending seven players home before the final match in Birmingham. Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq and Salman Ali Agha are among those dropped from the tour, while seven replacements have been brought into the squad.The changes have also extended to the coaching staff. Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and assistant coach Umar Gul have been released from their positions, with white-ball coach Mike Hesson set to take charge for the third Test.Ramiz believes the scale and timing of the overhaul could further damage the confidence of the Pakistan players rather than solve the team’s problems.“I'm trying to convince myself this is all OK, but it is not. It just shows Pakistan cricket has hit a panic button. It's not good for the game, it's not good for the confidence of the players who have come in, or for the players who are left, because it makes you a selfish team,” Ramiz, BBC Radio 5 Live.“What is the guarantee they will get the results? Some of these guys have not played Test cricket. I've got no idea why this was done,” he added.Ramiz questions unprecedented overhaulPakistan’s performances in England have been poor from the outset.They suffered an innings defeat in the opening Test at Headingley before England won the Lord’s Test by 194 runs. Across their four innings in the series, Pakistan have failed to reach 200 on every occasion.However, Ramiz questioned whether replacing such a large number of players midway through a tour could suddenly change the team’s fortunes.“I'm really not happy with the situation. How many times have we seen this happen in world cricket? Never, ever. This is more like football, midway through the season, firing a manager. If you ask me how things can be fixed, I've got no idea,” said Ramiz.The former PCB chairman also pointed to the uncertainty created for both the players being sent home and those suddenly brought into the squad.With the third Test fast approaching, several newcomers will be expected to adapt quickly to Test cricket and the conditions in England.Changes come amid Lord’s controversyThe PCB’s drastic decisions have come during an already turbulent tour.The Lord’s Test was played against the backdrop of an off-field dispute involving the sons of former Pakistan captain and prime minister Imran Khan.Sky Sports broadcast an interview with Suleiman and Kasim Khan during the lunch interval on the opening day. articles.title: 'Good for nothing': Danish Kaneria lambasts Pakistan cricket, calls it 'a shame after 70 years'
articles.summary: Cricket News: Former Pakistan spinner Danish Kaneria has strongly criticised the country’s cricket system after Pakistan suffered a 0-2 Test series defeat against E.
articles.body: Former Pakistan spinner Danish Kaneria has strongly criticised the country’s cricket system after Pakistan suffered a 0-2 Test series defeat against England. He questioned the team’s selection, coaching, domestic cricket structure and the lack of accountability within the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB).Pakistan’s 194-run loss at Lord’s gave England an unassailable lead in the series. In response, Pakistan released seven players from the squad and removed head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul. But Kaneria believes changing personnel will not solve the deeper problems.Kaneria questions Pakistan’s team and bowling attackKaneria said Pakistan’s cricket has lost its competitiveness and the fighting spirit that was once associated with the team. He also criticised the repeated changes in leadership and selection.“It's a shame that after 70 years, Pakistan has gone through such a disaster. There is no logic, selection committee, or play. They are just good for nothing. You see, such a bad performance. If a person loses, he tries and fights before losing. The fight has to be visible. Here, there’s no fight. No one knows anything,” he told news agency IANS.He also questioned why coaches and selectors are appointed for short periods before being removed, saying the system needs stability and people who are willing to take responsibility for both wins and losses.Kaneria was particularly unhappy with Pakistan’s bowling options. He pointed out that experienced players such as Mohammad Abbas, who took nine wickets at Lord’s, and spinner Noman Ali have been overlooked despite performing well.“And the bowling attack is pathetic. Who is Muhammad Shahzad? Where did he come from? He doesn’t have any line or length. No swing, no reverse swing. Nothing.”He also criticised Pakistan’s batting approach in English conditions, particularly the dismissals of Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan.“Like a player of the calibre of Babar Azam is getting out like this. This is pathetic. And then you are keeping Rizwan for so long. I don't know what he is doing. Why is he even there?”Call for major changes in domestic cricketKaneria believes the problems begin well before players reach the national team. He blamed the weakening of domestic cricket and the closure of departmental cricket for reducing the quality of Pakistan’s talent pool.“I like how the BCCI have put in their contracts that first class cricket is important. At least you play 5 to 6 games. None of our boys play domestic. And this downfall of Pakistan cricket started when the structure of domestic cricket changed.”He argued that selectors need to regularly watch domestic matches instead of relying heavily on performances in the Pakistan Super League.“The reason is that the talent pool has been eliminated. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former Sri Lanka captain Mahela Jayawardene is likely to continue as Mumbai Indians (MI) head coach for the 2027 edition of the Indian Premier League (IPL), with the franchise reluctant to make sweeping changes. It is learnt that Jayawardene joined the five-time champions on a "two + one" contract in 2024 and could well be given another year, considering it will be the last year of the ongoing cycle. A formal announcement is expected next month, provided there is no late change of heart.Under Jayawardene, Mumbai Indians reached the playoffs in 2025 but finished ninth the following year. 2026 was a disappointing season for the IPL giants, as they won only four games in a campaign marred by injuries, availability concerns and unrest in the dressing room.Since the disappointing last season, there has been a lot of chatter around their captain Hardik Pandya's potential trade. While multiple franchises have expressed interest, there has yet to be any substantial movement on that front.TimesofIndia.com has also learnt that some dialogue has taken place with the Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR), but the lack of a tradeable asset has not excited MI at the moment. Cameron Green's name was on the table, but the MI think tank is wary of the Australian's workload next year, which includes Australia's packed Test calendar. As far as the Chennai Super Kings (CSK) are concerned, some action is expected once they finalise their new head coach.Don't be surprised if he [Hardik Pandya] is not traded at all. Discussions have also happened with the player along these lines. For a trade to happen, multiple things need to fall into place. So it's not that straightforward.How will MI tackle the Pandya situation? They are keen on retaining him as a player for the upcoming season as they plan to head in a new direction under a new captain. The management has already explored this idea, and it is learnt that former India and MI captain Rohit Sharma is actively involved in discussions about the captaincy and the team's direction. Returning Rohit to the captaincy was also an option, but a new face is likely as the 39-year-old is not keen to wear the armband again. Tilak Varma and Jasprit Bumrah are two potential options, with the scales tilting in the former's favour."Don't be surprised if he is not traded at all. A change in captaincy is something they expect will restore normalcy, but navigating the turbulence will require significant effort. Another matter that will need attention is that of recently sacked India T20I captain Suryakumar Yadav. Apart from Pandya, there was chatter around the T20 specialist, but the franchise seems in no mood to let go of their experienced campaigner."Yes, he didn't have a good season last year, but what about the ones before that? MI will not discard a player based on one season, and that's not how they operate. They take pride in the 'One Family' tag and swear by it," adds the source.As things stand, continuity has been the bottom line. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former Pakistan captain Misbah-ul-Haq has offered his resignation from the Pakistan Cricket Board’s (PCB) national selection committee, adding another dramatic twist to the turmoil surrounding the Test side after a sweeping overhaul of the squad and coaching staff.According to Geo News, sources close to Misbah said the former cricketer had informed the PCB of his decision and would serve a notice period before formally stepping down. Cricinfo also reported that Misbah had offered his resignation, although the PCB is yet to accept it.The development comes just a day after the PCB announced wholesale changes to the Pakistan Test squad and coaching staff following the team’s heavy 194-run defeat to England at Lord’s.Misbah reportedly not consulted over sweeping changesThe timing of Misbah’s decision has raised questions over the selection committee’s role in the PCB’s latest overhaul. According to the reports, Misbah was apparently not consulted despite being part of the national selection committee when the board decided to make major changes to the squad and coaching staff.The PCB released seven players from the Test squad ahead of the third Test against England at Edgbaston, starting September 9. Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq, Salman Ali Agha, Ali Usman, Aamer Jamal, Awais Zafar and Khurram Shahzad were among those released.Sarfaraz Ahmed and Umar Gul were also removed as head coach and bowling coach respectively.The PCB subsequently brought in white-ball head coach Mike Hesson and bowling coach Ashley Noffke to work with the Test side for the remainder of the England tour.Cricinfo further reported that Misbah has decided to step down from his role as a batting consultant at the National Cricket Academy in Lahore, where his contract required him to work for 180 days a year.Five uncapped players brought into Test squadThe extent of Pakistan’s overhaul was further highlighted by the inclusion of five uncapped players in the squad for the third Test.Arafat Minhas, Mohammad Imran Jnr, Saad Baig, Mohammad Imran Randhawa and Razaullah have been added, while Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal have also been brought into the group.
