The back-to-back defeats left Pakistan 0-2 down in the three-match series and staring at a potential 3-0 clean sweep.Misbah’s latest exit from Pakistan cricket setupMisbah was appointed to the four-member national selection committee in March alongside Aaqib Javed, Sarfaraz Ahmed and Asad Shafiq.The former captain has previously held several senior positions within the PCB. He was appointed head coach and chief selector in 2019, before stepping down as chief selector in October 2020 and eventually leaving the head coach’s position in 2021.He returned to the PCB setup as an adviser in 2023 under the then ad hoc management committee headed by Zaka Ashraf. He was later appointed one of five mentors for the men’s Champions Cup and also worked with women’s domestic teams.Last month, Misbah coached the Pakistan Gold side to victory in the 50-over National Champions Cup in Multan under captain Shaheen Afridi.His reported resignation comes at a particularly difficult time for Pakistan cricket. The Lord’s defeat was their 15th loss in their last 20 Tests, while they currently sit at the bottom of the ICC World Test Championship 2025-27 standings.Pakistan squad for Birmingham Test against England: Babar Azam (captain), Abdullah Fazal, Arafat Minhas, Azan Awais, Mohammad Abbas, Mohammad Ali, Muhammad Imran, Mohammad Imran Jnr, Muhammad Ghazi Ghori (wk), Razaullah, Saad Baig (wicketkeeper), Saim Ayub, Sajid Khan, Saud Shakeel, Shan Masood, Abdullah Shafique, Ubaid Shah.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Pakistan v England: Shahid Afridi says seven changes 'most shocking decision ever'
articles.summary: Pakistan's decision to make dramatic changes to their squad during the series in England is the "most shocking decision ever", according to former captain Shahid Afridi.
articles.body:
Pakistan's decision to make wholesale changes to their squad and coaching set-up during the series in England has been branded the "most shocking decision ever by a selection committee" by former captain Shahid Afridi.

The tourists have dropped seven players and called up five uncapped players, while head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and his assistant Umar Gul have been replaced by Pakistan white-ball coach Mike Hesson and former Australia seamer Ashley Noffke.

Pakistan, who were thrashed in the opening two Tests, face England in the third and final match of the series at Edgbaston, starting on Wednesday, 9 September.

"Not sure what is the logic or reasoning behind this decision!", Afridi wrote on social media.

"Even the replacements make no sense - T20 players have been included for a Test match in England?

"What is this thinking and approach? Why has the coach been axed after five Test matches?

"This is the most shocking decision ever by a selection committee which includes so many experienced selectors."

Pakistan drop seven players and release head coach

Pakistan to meet King Charles after Lord's controversy

Five of the players dropped - Muhammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq, Salman Ali Agha, Ali Usman and Khurram Shahzad - have featured in the series so far, while Aamir Jamal and Muhammad Awais Jafar have been sent home without playing.

A total of seven players have been called up. Batters Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal have previous Test experience and join the quintet of uncapped newcomers.

Spin-bowling all-rounder Arafat Minhas, left-arm seamer Mohammed Imran Jr, wicketkeeper Said Baig and all-rounders Mohammad Imran and Razaullah have all received call-ups.

Ex-Pakistan captain Ramiz Raja, also a former chairman of the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) told BBC Radio 5 Live: "I'm trying to convince myself this is all OK, but it is not.

"It just shows Pakistan cricket has hit a panic button."

Pakistan are scheduled to have an audience with King Charles at Clarence House this week in an engagement that was planned before the series against England began.

However, it is set to take place despite the series almost coming to controversial early end during the second Test.

At lunch on the first day, the PCB threatened to cancel the remainder of the match and tour because of an interview with the sons of Imran Khan that was broadcast by Sky.

Imran, the former Pakistan captain and prime minster, has been in prison for three years on charges of corruption, which he denies.

Pakistan ultimately completed the Test, with both captain Babar Azam and head coach Sarfaraz denying any knowledge of a planned boycott.

articles.title: Ben Stokes: Former England Test captain signs for Adelaide Strikers in Big Bash League
articles.summary: Former England cricketer Ben Stokes will return to the Big Bash League this winter, joining the Adelaide Strikers for his first appearance in the franchise tournament since the 2014-15 season; Stokes retired from international cricket in June
articles.body:
Stokes will play in the franchise competition this winter after penning a one-year deal with the side following his retirement from international cricket.

It marks his return to the BBL for the first time in 12 years. He last played during the 2014-15 season for the Melbourne Renegades.

Stokes stunned the cricketing world when he announced his decision to step down as England's Test captain and retire from international cricket midway through his side's third Test against New Zealand in June.

The shock announcement came during the afternoon session on the fourth day of the series decider at Trent Bridge, with Stokes bowling when the news broke. He responded by taking a wicket with the very next ball.

His decision came after he was left out of the second Test against New Zealand following an investigation into an incident at a London nightclub.

He returned for the third Test, during which he made the decision to step down.

On making the decision to play in the BBL, Stokes said: "I'm really excited to be joining the Adelaide Strikers for BBL|16.

"I've always enjoyed playing in Australia, and when the opportunity came up to join the Strikers it was one I couldn't pass up.

"Adelaide Oval is an incredible place to play cricket, the Big Bash is a fantastic competition and the Strikers have an exciting group, so I'm looking forward to meeting the players, getting stuck in and contributing to a successful season.

"I can't wait to get started, create some special memories with the group and give Strikers fans plenty to cheer about."

Adelaide Strikers head coach Tim Paine said: "Ben is one of the greatest all-rounders the game has seen, a proven match-winner and a competitor who thrives under pressure.

"We're thrilled to have a player of his ability join our squad and can't wait to see him put on a show in BBL|16.

"Our fans have watched him produce some of the most memorable moments over the past decade, and now they'll have the chance to see him in Strikers blue.

"Adelaide Oval is the best place in the world to play and watch cricket, so we're looking forward to seeing our members and fans flock through the gates to watch him in action."

articles.body: The Pakistan Cricket Board’s (PCB) stunning overhaul of the Test squad and coaching staff has become a major talking point in the cricket world, with Multan Sultans CEO Gohar Shah joining the growing chorus of criticism surrounding the changes.The PCB released seven players from the Test squad ahead of the third Test against England at Edgbaston, beginning September 9. I was a fan before I was a stakeholder."Things I’ve observed from my playing days + actively being involved with the PSL, dressing room and PCB leadership," he wrote.Shah then raised concerns over professionalism among players, including diet, workload and attitude."Late nights and junk food are common. Now I understand living on hotel food and being stuck for 6 weeks is tough, but the word “professional” has to mean something," he wrote.He also questioned the intensity shown by players during Test matches."No one wants to do the tough yards. It’s a mentality thing. Like for instance a few times in the test match after a long spell the pace bowlers didn’t run after the ball. What are you saving your legs for? The test match ended in 2.5 days…"‘Job first, Pakistan later’Shah also turned his attention to Pakistan’s wider cricket ecosystem, including journalists, former players and the PCB.On the media, he wrote: "Journalists all pushing their own agendas, And they build narratives on who they like / who caters for them more I.e these things may or may not be leaks , gifts, favours."He was equally critical of former players who comment on the game without taking up coaching roles."Barring a few who actually worked and got their coaching badges and qualifications most find it more comfortable to go on tv and just iterate the problems. No one presents the solutions nor goes out there and gets the experience / qualifications to contribute."Shah reserved another strong observation for the PCB, writing: "The board is too bureaucratic. Everyone fears to speak their mind because they worry about backlash and their jobs."He added: "There are people that genuinely wanted to help , but when they see their efforts go no where they stop trying and just settle for their paycheck."‘Pakistan cricket will always be in my heart’Shah also questioned the structure surrounding Pakistan Super League franchises, arguing that owners have limited incentives to invest heavily in developing their teams."10 year lease, you grow the brand, only to give it back to the PCB. So why would you grow if you see none of the benefit? Only the bills."He also questioned retention rules and category changes, saying owners "invest in players and talent hunts only to lose them due to retention rules and category changes that are agenda driven."Shah ended his post with a message of hope despite his criticism."Pakistan cricket will always be in my heart. Pray for us to go back to being the best. Not just good or competitive, but the best."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘Hope is still alive’: Krunal Pandya reacts after missing out on India’s Afghanistan T20I squad
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Krunal Pandya has hinted that his hopes of returning to international cricket remain alive after the all-rounder was left out of India’s sq.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Krunal Pandya has hinted that his hopes of returning to international cricket remain alive after the all-rounder was left out of India’s squad for the upcoming three-match T20I series against Afghanistan.Shortly after the squad was announced on Tuesday, Krunal shared a poignant message on social media, writing: “Hope is still alive”.The 35-year-old left-arm spinner has been pushing for a return to India’s T20I setup and, as reported earlier by TimesofIndia.com, had emerged as an option for the selectors following India’s recent outings in Ireland and England.Afghanistan will host India for three T20Is in New Delhi on September 13, 15 and 17, with the Arun Jaitley Stadium set to stage all three matches.Krunal misses out despite strong IPL seasonKrunal last played for India in the 2021 T20I series against Sri Lanka but has remained on the selectors’ radar following an impressive IPL 2026 campaign.Playing for Royal Challengers Bengaluru, Krunal picked up 14 wickets during the season and once again showcased his value as a left-arm spin-bowling all-rounder.India have been exploring options in that department after their recent T20I assignments. Axar Patel featured in all seven matches against Ireland and England, but managed only four wickets — two in the two T20Is against Ireland and two in four games against England.The selectors opted against recalling him for the Afghanistan series.His social media message suggests he remains hopeful of another opportunity with India.Bumrah returns, several players subject to fitnessPace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah has returned to the squad for the Afghanistan series, although his selection is subject to fitness clearance.Bumrah had been sidelined after sustaining an impact injury to his knee during India’s ODI series in England. He subsequently missed the two-Test series in Sri Lanka after being advised rest by the BCCI medical team.Nitish Kumar Reddy, Washington Sundar and Harshit Rana have also been included subject to fitness clearance. All three have recently dealt with injuries and are currently under Return to Play protocols.Rana suffered a Grade 1 hamstring injury during India’s third T20I against England, while Washington sustained a hamstring injury during the third ODI against England. Reddy had also been recovering from an injury that ruled him out of India’s recent assignments.As reported earlier by TimesofIndia.com, Hardik Pandya has also missed out after a late leg niggle disrupted his comeback plans at the BCCI Centre of Excellence. He has not played competitive cricket since turning out for Mumbai Indians on May 24, while his last appearance for India came in the T20 World Cup final on March 8.India Squad for Afghanistan T20IsShreyas Iyer (c), Abhishek Sharma, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Sanju Samson (wk), Ishan Kishan (wk), Tilak Varma (vc), Shivam Dube, Nitish Kumar Reddy*, Axar Patel, Washington Sundar*, Varun Chakaravarthy, Ravi Bishnoi, Jasprit Bumrah*, Arshdeep Singh, Harshit Rana*.(*Subject to fitness clearance)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asian Games cricket row: Japan Cricket CEO says teams can make own arrangements
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: With concerns over accommodation and other logistical arrangements emerging ahead of cricket’s return to the Asian Games, Japan Cricket Ass.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: With concerns over accommodation and other logistical arrangements emerging ahead of cricket’s return to the Asian Games, Japan Cricket Association (JCA) CEO Naoki Alex Miyaji has sought to put the apprehensions into perspective, saying participating teams have been offered hotel accommodation but are free to make their own arrangements.At a recent Asian Cricket Council (ACC) meeting, leading cricketing nations reportedly raised concerns over the accommodation arrangements, with the designated hotel located around 20km from the Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin City, Aichi Prefecture, where the cricket matches will be held.The Asian Games begin on September 17.Japan Cricket CEO clarifies accommodation arrangementsMiyaji stressed that the JCA is playing a limited role in the event’s organisation.“The Asian Games is being organised by the organising committee Aichi-Nagoya Games Organizing Committee (AINAGOC) in collaboration with the ACC under the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA),” Miyaji told PTI.“The JCA has provided support in some areas but is not directly involved so I am not able to directly answer all of your questions. What I can say is that all parties are working hard to ensure the success of Cricket in the Asian Games.“I can also assure you that the ACC have been discussing accommodation options with AINAGOC for a long time. The participating teams in cricket are being offered hotel accommodation,” he said.Miyaji also pointed out that cricket is not the only sport facing logistical constraints at the Games.“Many other sports are being accommodated in much more limited facilities such as a cruise ship or container hotels. The teams are free to arrange their own accommodation if they chose to do so,” he said.‘Toilets will be available within the player area’Miyaji also sought to allay concerns over reports that team washrooms could be located at least half a kilometre from the playing arena.“Please note that toilets will be available within the player area. There are both temporary and permanent facilities at the venue. The facilities on the ground are temporary, but AINAGOC have worked very closely with the ACC for over a year now to ensure that the best facilities are provided within the limited timeline and facility restrictions,” Miyaji said.He also addressed concerns over the makeshift dressing rooms being prepared for the tournament.“Despite being temporary, the facilities will provide as comfortable a space as possible for the players and officials. There are also permanent facilities around the ground which will be available to the players,” he said.Korogi Sports Park built from scratchMiyaji explained that organisers had only 17 months to prepare the venue, which had to be developed from scratch because Aichi Prefecture did not have an established cricket facility.“They only had 17 months to prepare and had to start from scratch as there were no Cricket venues of any standard in Aichi Prefecture. Considering the limited time and resources available, AINAGOC and ACC have worked together to ensure that the playing facilities are suitable,” he said.Sri Lanka Cricket has also provided curators to work on the turf and hybrid pitches.“It will be a full size ground with turf and hybrid pitches prepared by the best curators which Sri Lanka Cricket should be credited for providing,” Miyaji said.“There are limits on what they can do within these tight limits, but from what I have seen, the playing surface and field will be the best seen in Cricket's inclusion in the Asian Games.”The JCA, meanwhile, has concentrated largely on building local interest in the sport.“We have taken cricket to many school and shopping centres which have received great enthusiasm. Thanks to the full support of Nisshin City, we are confident that the local community will be 100% behind the Asian Games.”Miyaji remained confident that cricket would make a strong impression when the continental event is staged in Japan.“Cricket will be one of the largest sports in the Asian Games. It will also be the first time the top Cricket teams of Asia will be playing in Japan,” he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi stars as East Zone beat defending champions to reach Duleep Trophy final
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s aggressive cameo, backed by fiery spells from Mohammed Shami and Mukesh Kumar, helped East Zone storm into the Dulee.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s aggressive cameo, backed by fiery spells from Mohammed Shami and Mukesh Kumar, helped East Zone storm into the Duleep Trophy final with a four-wicket win over defending champions Central Zone on Tuesday.The 15-year-old Sooryavanshi made a valuable contribution of 40 off 43 balls as East Zone chased down a target of 159 on a turning pitch on the third day of the semifinal.East, winners of the tournament in the 2012-13 season, will face either South Zone or North Zone in the final at Chepauk from September 6.Sooryavanshi provides early spark before dramatic dismissalChasing 159, East needed a steady start as the pitch increasingly aided the spinners. Sooryavanshi initially adopted a cautious approach, scoring his first 15 runs from 30 balls.But once he found his rhythm, the left-hander shifted gears spectacularly. His next 25 runs came from just 13 deliveries, featuring another six and three boundaries.His opening partner Abhimanyu Easwaran was more fluent initially, including a six off off-spinner Saransh Jain over long-on, while Sooryavanshi struggled to find the same freedom against spin.The teenager, however, came alive when Yash Thakur was introduced into the attack. Having already hammered the pacer for four fours and two sixes in the first innings, Sooryavanshi again went after him, smashing three fours and a six in the 14th over.But his attacking approach also brought about his downfall. Sooryavanshi fell in the same over when Rajat Patidar completed a stunning running catch off Thakur.His dismissal suddenly changed the mood of the chase, with East losing wickets at regular intervals. Harsh Dubey then struck twice in successive deliveries, removing Kumar Kushagra and Anukul Roy to leave East at 124 for five.Shami, Mukesh dismantle Central before Kishan finishes chaseEarlier, Central resumed their second innings at 45 for three but suffered a dramatic collapse in the extended first session. They lost their remaining seven wickets to be bowled out for 158.Shami and Mukesh were the chief destroyers, exploiting variable bounce and the assistance available to the bowlers. Shami finished with 3/56, while Mukesh claimed 4/44 to complete a seven-wicket haul in the match.Mukesh was subsequently named Player of the Match, providing a timely boost to the India seamer who has been out of favour.Central briefly threatened to stretch the chase when Dubey and Arshad Khan added 43 for the ninth wicket, taking their side beyond 150. But East held their nerve to complete the victory.Ishan Kishan then produced a composed 39 not out from 41 balls to guide East home with minimal further trouble.“For a personal point of view, and not only me, the entire team members are looking forward to playing in the final. It will be heartening if we can go on and win that title,” Easwaran said after the match.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Alice Capsey: England wicketkeeper impresses in first ODI win over Ireland after 'rogue' switch behind the stumps
articles.summary: Watch second ODI between England and Ireland in Derby on Thursday, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 12.30pm (1pm start)
articles.body:
England's call to have Capsey keep wicket for their one-day international series against Ireland divided opinion, despite her impressing with both bat and gloves in the opening six-wicket win in Leicester on Tuesday .

Capsey claimed a terrific diving catch for the opening breakthrough and conceded only four byes - off a bizarre Issy Wong delivery that deflected off the stumps and to the boundary - before her unbeaten 41 off 40 balls saw England over the line.

Former England bowler Tash Farrant spoke of the reasoning behind the home side's call to bring Capsey in for regular wicketkeeper Amy Jones.

"It is a rogue move, as she hasn't really done any keeping for about three or four years, but she is a pretty good athlete and has good hands in the field," Farrant told Sky Sports Cricket .

"I have no doubt that, if she was to put her mind to it, she could be a decent wicketkeeper, so England are seeing if this is a viable option.

"Kira Chathli and Ellie Threlkeld are good with the gloves but are they good enough with the bat?"

Former Ireland international Isobel Joyce added: "I'm surprised England are doing it in a one-day international.

"Why not do it in a T20? You get so much of the ball as a keeper in a 50-over game, so it seems crazy to me that you'd do it for the first time in an ODI.

"You've got to repeat your good processes so many times. It's a big uptaking for her."

Capsey impresses on first England outing with gloves

Capsey proved up to the task, however, hardly putting a foot wrong during the hosts' 50 overs in the field as Ireland posted an ODI-best versus England of 281-5.

There was also her impressive, one-handed grab to see the back or Ireland opener Alice Tector in the fifth over of their innings.

"It's a good catch," Sky Sports Cricket's Dominic Cork said. "It's one of those ones where you could perhaps leave it and say to first slip, 'you take it'.

"But Capsey said 'no, I'm going to have that' and took it one-handed. All of the questions about her answered. A nice grab."

He added: "I don't mind it [Capsey as wicketkeeper], just to add a little bit more depth in the batting.

"It's not an easy job though. It will be interesting to see how she gets on.

"When you watch some of the best wicketkeepers around, like Amy Jones, Sarah Taylor, Ben Foakes - even going back to Jack Russell - it's about having quick hands."

Capsey gave further demonstration of those quick hands of hers and lightning reflexes when claiming a neat take later in the innings, stood up to the stumps off Wong.

Sky Sports Cricket's Ravi Bopara said at the time: "That is an excellent take, especially off a bowler like Wong who has been nipping the ball back most of the time.

"This ball stood up and Capsey got her body out of the way so she could get her hands up high enough."

Too great a workload for Sciver-Brunt successor?

But despite Capsey's strong showing with the gloves, there were still some concerns raised, particularly centred around the 22-year-old's increased workload.

"She's going to be feeling it in those legs," Farrant said. "Batting at number four as well, she's really been thrown into it today.

"She hasn't kept for a very long time in a game, let alone a 50-over match. You maybe would have been expecting her to be down at five or six - but she's in the thick of it at four."

Capsey looked fresh enough when cracking four boundaries and a six in her 40-ball 41 that helped fire England to their record ODI chase with 71 balls remaining.

But it's precisely Capsey's batting that Sky Sports Cricket's Charles Dagnall would prefer was her sole focus.

"The decision to pick Capsey as a wicketkeeper is not for me. I don't see it as a long-term option, so I'm wondering why England are doing it," he said.

"She did really well today, took a great catch, and hardly gave away any byes.

"But what is the primary role of Capsey? It is to be one of England's best batters.

"She is one of our brightest batting prospects and only 22. I see her as the long-term replacement for Nat Sciver-Brunt. She is that vital to England."

articles.title: Lhuan-dre Pretorius stars as South Africa beat Zimbabwe again to strengthen tri-series campaign
articles.summary: Cricket News: South Africa continued their strong run in the Namibia T20I Tri-Series with another convincing victory over Zimbabwe, securing a comfortable 43-run wi.
articles.body: South Africa continued their strong run in the Namibia T20I Tri-Series with another convincing victory over Zimbabwe, securing a comfortable 43-run win in the fourth match at the Namibia Cricket Ground on Tuesday.Lhuan-dre Pretorius narrowly missed out on a maiden T20I century but produced a career-best 94 to set up South Africa’s second victory over Zimbabwe in the tournament. The opener’s sensational knock came off just 51 balls and featured 12 fours and three sixes.Pretorius was named Player of the Match after helping South Africa post 185/7 before their bowlers completed the job by dismissing Zimbabwe for 142 in 17.4 overs.Pretorius powers South Africa to 185Put into bat, South Africa made an aggressive start, with Pretorius anchoring the innings and playing a key role in two partnerships of more than 50 runs for the first two wickets.He found an able partner in Dewald Brevis, who struck 41 off 27 balls, as the Proteas built a strong platform. Zimbabwe did manage to fight back with regular wickets towards the latter stages, but South Africa had already done enough damage to reach a competitive 185/7.Pretorius fell six runs short of a century, but the opener insisted the team victory mattered more than his individual milestone.“Yeah, that's fine. I'm just glad we got over the line. Milestones will come and go, and yeah, it wasn't meant to be today, but I was just glad because we said at the 14-over mark we wanted to get to 200, and I knew if I got the team to 200 I'd get to the milestone. But yeah, I think milestones come and go, and today was not meant to be, but we won, so it's good,” Pretorius said.Jansen, Fortuin dismantle Zimbabwe chaseZimbabwe needed 186 for victory but struggled to maintain momentum after a promising beginning from Brian Bennett.Their powerplay was derailed by a double-wicket maiden from captain Bjorn Fortuin, and South Africa struck again soon after the fielding restrictions ended.Duan Jansen produced a decisive burst, taking three wickets in four balls across two overs to leave Zimbabwe in serious trouble.Captain Sikandar Raza offered some resistance with 45 off 33 balls, while Newman Nyamhuri added 27 with some aggressive hitting. But the pair could only reduce the eventual margin of defeat as Zimbabwe were bowled out for 142.Fortuin was the standout bowler, finishing with 4/24 from 3.4 overs, while Jansen claimed 3/21. articles.title: Pakistan cricket chaos: PCB seeks answers over Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq picks as Misbah-ul-Haq quits selection committee
articles.summary: Cricket News: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has sought an explanation from its national selection committee over the inclusion of Mohammad Rizwan and Imam-ul-Haq.
articles.body: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has sought an explanation from its national selection committee over the inclusion of Mohammad Rizwan and Imam-ul-Haq in the Test squad for the ongoing England series, adding another layer to the turmoil surrounding the side.According to a report by Geo News, the PCB issued a notice to members of the selection committee on August 31, asking them to explain the basis and rationale behind recommending Rizwan and Imam for the Test squad.The notice, a copy of which was seen by Geo News, directed committee members including Aqib Javed, Misbah-ul-Haq and Asad Shafiq to submit written explanations detailing the players’ performances, selection criteria and other factors considered during the process. The members have been given 24 hours from receipt of the notice to respond.PCB questions selection processThe notice reportedly referred specifically to a selection committee meeting held on June 2, 2026. The minutes of that meeting were submitted on July 1, with members tasked with considering players for Pakistan’s Test squads for the tours of the West Indies and England.Rizwan and Imam were subsequently shortlisted on the committee members’ recommendations.The PCB’s move comes after Pakistan endured a disastrous start to the three-match Test series against England. They suffered an innings-and-103-run defeat in the opening Test before going down by 194 runs at Lord’s, handing England an unassailable 2-0 lead.Both Rizwan and Imam were subsequently released from the Test squad ahead of the third match at Edgbaston, beginning September 9.Misbah set to step down amid overhaulThe PCB’s demand for an explanation comes amid a sweeping overhaul of the Pakistan Test setup.A day before the notice emerged, the board announced that seven players had been released from the squad. Alongside Rizwan and Imam, Salman Ali Agha, Ali Usman, Aamir Jamal, Muhammad Awais Zafar and Khurram Shahzad were also sent out.Pakistan have brought in seven replacements, including Test-capped batters Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal, while Arafat Minhas, Mohammad Imran Jnr, Saad Baig, Mohammad Imran and Razaullah have also been added.The coaching staff has undergone a major change as well, with head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul removed from their positions. White-ball head coach Mike Hesson and bowling coach Ashley Noffke have been brought in to oversee the side for the remainder of the England tour.The developments have also triggered uncertainty within the selection committee itself. Sources close to Misbah-ul-Haq said he has decided to resign from the committee, informing the PCB of his decision and agreeing to serve a notice period before formally stepping down.The former Pakistan captain’s reported decision adds another twist to an already chaotic period for Pakistan cricket, with the board now seeking answers from the very selection process that produced a squad it has subsequently overhauled midway through the England series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: England v Ireland: Maia Bouchier ton sets up hosts' record ODI run chase
articles.summary: Maia Bouchier's stunning century helps England women seal their record one-day international chase of 282 to beat Ireland in the series opener.
articles.body:
First ODI, Uptonsteel County Ground, Leicester

Ireland 281-5 (50 overs): Lewis 69 (89), Hunter 62 (90), Stokell 54* (48)

England 283-4 (38.1 overs): Bouchier 104 (95), Dunkley 73 (61); Murray 3-58

England won by six wickets; lead series 1-0

England's new era started with a dominant six-wicket win over Ireland as they cruised to their record chase of 282 in the first one-day international.

Opener Maia Bouchier struck a stunning 104 off 95 balls to secure England's highest chase in women's ODIs with 11.5 overs to spare.

Bouchier added 143 for the first wicket with Sophia Dunkley, who made 73, which laid the perfect platform before the centurion holed out to long-on with just 59 runs needed.

Alice Capsey and Freya Kemp made light work of those remaining runs with a quickfire stand of 54 off 38 balls to put England within touching distance, Capsey hitting the winning boundary to finish unbeaten on 41.

Ireland were poor with the ball and sloppy in the field, but nevertheless it was a brilliant start for England's transitional batting line-up, which is without the recently retired Heather Knight and Tammy Beaumont, and in the absence of injured captain Nat Sciver-Brunt.

Despite their struggles in the field, Ireland earlier impressed with the bat to post 281-5, with half-centuries for captain Gaby Lewis, Amy Hunter and Rebecca Stokell.

Lewis and Hunter added 136 for the second wicket before Stokell's counter-attacking knock of 54 not out from 48 balls provided a late boost, as England's bowlers lacked threat in the middle overs, without Lauren Bell and Sophie Ecclestone, who are being rested.

It looked a competitive total at the halfway mark, but on a flat pitch offering little assistance for the bowlers, the gulf in class and experience was stark in the second innings.

The three-match series continues at Derby on Thursday.

'It's an unknown' - Capsey takes England gloves for first time

Ireland women in England 2026 Published 1 hour ago

Bouchier and Dunkley's statement innings

Both Bouchier and Dunkley are familiar faces in England shirts, but neither has really nailed down a place in the ODI XI despite plenty of opportunities.

But with the retirements of Beaumont and Knight, two of England's finest, head coach Charlotte Edwards is building towards next summer's Ashes with places up for grabs in the top order.

Edwards and the batters know tougher tests will come - only Orla Prendergast in Ireland's line-up offers a similar threat to the world's best bowlers - but both Dunkley and Bouchier made their cases at the first time of asking.

Bouchier started watchfully, making just eight off her first 19 balls, before a flurry of boundaries off medium-pacer Jane Maguire in the sixth over kickstarted her knock.

England reached 72-0 in the powerplay, with Bouchier playing second fiddle to Dunkley, who was brutal against Ireland's wilting bowling attack in a 47-ball fifty - her fastest in ODIs.

Dunkley was caught and bowled off Cara Murray in the 20th over but Bouchier held her nerve. She took ownership as Jodi Grewcock, the new face in England's line-up, looked nervous for her nine before finding the perfect company from Capsey's proactive approach.

Bouchier looked disappointed when she was caught at long-on after a lapse of concentration, but Kemp and Capsey ensured her efforts were not wasted - the former whacked 36 off 22 to show the power of England's rapidly-improving depth, with five batters missing from the team that started the 50-over World Cup semi-final last year.

Though there are concerns for Ireland's bowling as the series continues, it was a promising start to the series for their batters as England's own bowling attack looked unthreatening without the class and experience of Bell and Ecclestone.

Wong struck early to dismiss Alice Tector for 11 with assistance from a fine one-handed catch from Capsey, who is deputising for Amy Jones as wicketkeeper and showed promised with the gloves. But overall Wong was too inconsistent, bowling five wides in her spell.

Stand-in skipper Charlie Dean held things together with 2-44 but it was a tough outing for young left-arm spinner Tilly Corteen-Coleman, who bowled seven wicketless overs for 53 as the pitch offered little.

Ireland are heavily reliant on Lewis and all-rounder Prendergast, and when the latter fell for 19 after Lewis' knock of 69, there was a worry that their solid platform would be wasted.

But Stokell's dynamic knock appeared to take England by surprise as she struck the ball cleanly down the ground with regularity, and she even had to celebrate reaching fifty twice after the umpire mistakenly gave her runs for a boundary that had come off her pad.

She did eventually reach the milestone in a fifth-wicket stand of 84 with Leah Paul, but England's approach showed they would have needed a total beyond 300 to be challenging.

With two games to go, it feels like further records could be broken - especially if England are tasked with batting first.

articles.title: England beat Ireland in first ODI as Maia Bouchier scores century in team's highest run chase in the format
articles.summary: Maia Bouchier scores second ODI hundred as England reach target of 282 with 71 balls to spare to take 1-0 lead in three-match series; home side - who have rested key players including Nat Sciver-Brunt - sloppy with the ball and in the field; second ODI in Derby on Thursday (1pm start)
articles.body:
Maia Bouchier (104 off 95) and Sophia Dunkley (73 off 61) smoked 143 for the opening wicket inside 20 overs before Bouchier went on to notch her second ODI ton as England reached their target of 282 with 71 balls to spare.

Freya Kemp (36 off 22) drilled four fours in a row off Arlene Kelly in the 34th over - a feat Bouchier had managed off Jane Maguire towards the start of the chase - as the all-rounder dominated a 54-run partnership from 38 balls with Alice Capsey (41no off 40), after Capsey and Bouchier added 50 off 47.

England's previous record ODI run chase was the 267-8 they knocked off against Australia in Bristol during the home Ashes in 2023, a game in which Heather Knight and Tammy Beaumont posted the two highest scores.

With Knight and Beaumont now retired and team stalwarts Nat Sciver-Brunt, Danni Wyatt-Hodge and Amy Jones rested for this three-match assignment, Dunkley and Bouchier played the key roles, albeit aided by some error-strewn stuff from Ireland.

The tourists offered up way too many boundary balls and were also guilty of mis-fields - a blemish on the deep midwicket fence allowed Capsey to pump the winning four - as they slipped 1-0 down in a series that continues in Derby on Thursday (1pm) and then concludes in Worcester on Sunday (10.30am).

Capsey excels as wicketkeeper - but England scruffy in the field

England had been sloppy themselves in the Ireland innings, shipping 20 wides and 33 extras in total in the absence of spinner Sophie Ecclestone and seamer Lauren Bell, who, like captain Sciver-Brunt, Jones and Wyatt-Hodge, have been given these games off.

However, Capsey excelled as she kept wicket with Jones missing, taking a one-handed catch to her right in the fifth over and looking slick with the gloves throughout - if that continues over the next two matches, Jones' place could perhaps be in jeopardy moving forward.

Stand-in skipper Charlie Dean (2-44) was the pick of the bowlers, although Issy Wong (2-57) broke the 136-run stand between Ireland captain Gaby Lewis (69) and Amy Hunter (62) for the second wicket when she bowled the former through the gate.

Wong had made a scruffy start around nicking off Lewis' fellow opener Alice Tector (11) - the sister of men's Ireland internationals Harry and Tim Tector - sending down four wides outside off stump in a row in her third over of the game.

Lewis and Hunter, who ran superbly around hitting boundaries, propelled Ireland from 13-1 to 149-1, but the away side then lost three wickets for 35 runs once Lewis fell, with Hunter castled by Dean and Orla Prendergast (19) heaving Mady Villiers (1-46) to deep midwicket, where Bouchier claimed a terrific diving catch.

Ireland impress with the bat but well beaten in the end

Ireland rallied again through Rebecca Stokell (54no) and Leah Paul (29) putting on 84 from 71 balls for the fifth wicket, although the tourists only managed 24 runs, and no boundaries off the bat, across the final four overs shared by Dean and Wong.

Ireland did, however, earn four byes in Wong's final over when a ball thudded into Stokell's leg stump and raced away for four as the bails, somehow, stayed on.

The visitors' total looked a daunting one at halfway, particularly with England missing some senior batters, but the slapdash bowling and fielding meant the hosts were never really under pressure once the innings got going.

Ireland leg-spinner Cara Murray (3-58) caught and bowled Dunkley and cleaned up the inexperienced Jodi Grewcock (9) with a beautifully flighted delivery to reduce England to 173-2 in the 24th over, while Bouchier holed out off Kelly in the 32nd with 59 runs required.

Kemp was the final batter to fall, caught off Murray at deep midwicket looking to seal victory with a booming six.

Dean: England could have been tighter with the ball

England captain Charlie Dean , speaking at the presentation:

"It was amazing to chase a high total like that down, and the way that we did it - it's credit to the girls. Trying to take on the opening powerplay in 50-over cricket feels like good blueprint to have.

"Sophia and Maia did that remarkably, and didn't slow down after the powerplay, extending the partnership. For Maia to get a hundred was exceptional.

"We probably could have been a little tighter with the ball, to be honest, but to manage to restrict them, put on a performance like that and win in the end was brilliant.

"I can't fault the girls [for their fielding]. It wasn't for a lack of trying, but I think we can definitely sharpen up in the field and with the ball."

articles.title: Sanju Samson, Jasprit Bumrah return for Afghanistan T20I series; Hardik Pandya unfit
articles.summary: Cricket News: MUMBAI: Hardik Pandya's comeback to India T20I side has been delayed again, with the star all-rounder yet to regain full fitness. However, Sanju Samso.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Hardik Pandya's comeback to India T20I side has been delayed again, with the star all-rounder yet to regain full fitness. However, Sanju Samson, pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah and mystery spinner Varun Chakravarthy have returned as India named a near-full-strength squad for the three-match T20I series against Afghanistan in Delhi from Sept 13-17.Bumrah, who last played a T20I in India's T20 World Cup final win over New Zealand on March 8, has been included subject to fitness after a recurrence of a left knee injury forced him to miss the final ODI in England at Lord's and the subsequent Test series in Sri Lanka. Shreyas Iyer will continue as captain, with Tilak Varma serving as vice-captain.Samson, rested for Zimbabwe series, returns as one of two specialist wicketkeepers alongside Ishan Kishan. He is among eight changes from that squad, with Rinku Singh, Suryansh Shedge, Harsh Dubey, Prabhsimran Singh, Prince Yadav, Yash Thakur, Mayank Yadav and Ashok Sharma making way.Apart from Bumrah, Washington Sundar, Nitish Kumar Reddy and Harshit Rana have also been selected subject to clearance from BCCI Centre of Excellence. Varun, too, has returned after recovering from a hamstring injury sustained on England tour. "Four cricketers have been picked subject to fitne-ss. We will know about their fitness status for this series before Sept 9," BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia told TOI.Reddy has been undergoing rehabilitation for a quadriceps injury suffered during the ODI series against Afghanistan and has not played a T20I since Jan. Sundar has been recovering from a hamstring strain that ruled him out of Sri Lanka Tests.Hardik's absence remains the biggest talking point. The all-rounder has not played since India's T20 World Cup triumph in March, while his last competitive outing came for Mumbai Indians in IPL 2026 on May 24. A leg strain, sustained shortly after he was initially picked, ruled him out of Ireland and England white-ball tours and continues to keep him sidelined.Shedge, Prince Yadav and Prasidh Krishna, who featured on England tour, have also missed out on selection for Afghanistan series.Squad: India's squad: Shreyas Iyer (C), Abhishek Sharma, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Sanju Samson WK, Ishan Kishan WK, Tilak Varma VC, Shivam Dube, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Washington Sundar, Varun Chakravarthy, Ravi Bishnoi, Jasprit Bumrah, Arshdeep Singh, Harshit Rana.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India A to play three four-day matches against New Zealand: All you need to know
articles.summary: Cricket News: New Zealand will host India A for three four-day matches in Christchurch from October 24, giving the players valuable preparation ahead of the senior .
articles.body: New Zealand will host India A for three four-day matches in Christchurch from October 24, giving the players valuable preparation ahead of the senior teams’ two-Test series later in the year.New Zealand Cricket (NZC) confirmed the fixtures while announcing the schedule for the country’s domestic Plunket Shield competition. The three matches will be played alongside India’s white-ball tour of New Zealand.India are set to tour New Zealand from October to December for a busy multi-format assignment featuring five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests. The India A matches will give players an opportunity to adapt to New Zealand conditions before the Test series."The domestic red ball summer will also get an injection of international class as New Zealand A host India A for three four-day matches in Christchurch starting October 24," NZC said in a statement.The exact dates of the three India A matches have not yet been announced, but all three fixtures will be held in Christchurch. The senior India team’s white-ball campaign will begin on October 22 with the first T20I in Christchurch.The five T20Is will be played from October 22 to November 1, followed by five ODIs from November 4 to 15. The Test series will then begin on November 19.India return to New Zealand for TestsThe first Test will be played in Wellington from November 19 to 23, while the second Test is scheduled in Christchurch from November 27 to December 1.The tour will be a significant one for both teams. India will play Test cricket in New Zealand for the first time since 2019, while their last white-ball assignment in the country came in 2022.New Zealand Cricket also confirmed that its domestic first-class season will run from November 19 to March 29, with a break during the Super Smash and Ford Trophy competitions.India tour of New Zealand 20261st T20I: October 22, Christchurch2nd T20I: October 24, Christchurch3rd T20I: October 27, Wellington4th T20I: October 30, Auckland5th T20I: November 1, Hamilton1st ODI: November 4, Auckland2nd ODI: November 7, Wellington3rd ODI: November 10, Hamilton4th ODI: November 13, Mount Maunganui5th ODI: November 15, Mount Maunganui1st Test: November 19-23, Wellington2nd Test: November 27-December 1, ChristchurchGet the latest Sports News and Live updates.
